# AA Prototype — PROGRESS

The running record of the build. **Every phase session reads this file first and updates it last.**
It holds the binding conventions, the status of every phase, the decisions log, and a per-phase
entry describing what was *actually* built (which may differ from the plan — record the truth).

Statuses: NOT STARTED → IN PROGRESS → DONE (with date). If a phase is partially done at the end
of a session, leave it IN PROGRESS and state exactly what remains.

## Binding conventions (all phases)

1. **App location.** The app lives in `aa-prototype/` at the repo root. Docs live in `docs/prototype-build/`. Never create a second app folder.
2. **Stack is fixed.** Vite + React 18 + TypeScript (strict, no `any`), React Router, Zustand for the store, Tailwind CSS + a design-token layer (`src/theme/`), lucide-react icons, date-fns, Vitest for unit tests. No additional UI framework without a decisions-log entry.
3. **Folder shape.** `src/domain/` (types, seed, billing maths, validators — pure, no React), `src/store/` (Zustand slices, lifecycle guards, audit writer), `src/apps/mobile/`, `src/apps/web/`, `src/apps/admin/`, `src/apps/demo/` (demo-only surfaces: control panel, Xero sim, integrations, billing monitor), `src/shared/` (cross-app components), `src/shell/` (app switcher, phone frame, layout).
4. **Mock backend only.** Components never own domain state; they read/write through typed store hooks. No `fetch`, no real endpoints. Simulated external systems (Xero, HL7, PDF/OCR) are store actions, registered in `src/shared/demoTriggers` and shown on their screen (harness bar "Demo actions" menu or the PWA's Demo sheet); the demo control panel is their index, and demo screens may also host them.
5. **Deterministic seed.** All seed data generated from a seeded RNG + pinned demo date (`DEMO_TODAY`, 2026-07-21 — the design mockups' content date, see Decisions log). Same seed → identical data. Reset restores the pristine seed. Never call `Date.now()`/`new Date()` for domain logic — use the demo clock.
6. **Lifecycle rules live in the store.** ACTIVE → SUBMITTED → AUTHORISED transitions are guarded functions; SUBMITTED strips anaesthetist edit rights; AUTHORISED locks Cards immutable; there is **no Returned state**. UI can never bypass a guard. *Renamed from DRAFT in Phase 15b (EP-07, FT-07.1, 2026-10-07); DRAFT now means a Draft List with no anaesthetist and arrives in Phase 31.*
7. **Audit is append-only.** Every Card/Procedure mutation (and List reassignment/state change) writes an audit entry `{who, role, source, action, before→after, at}`. No mutation without one.
8. **NHI never crosses to Xero.** Xero-sim screens and data show only the hidden internal ID (ContactNumber) and ContactID. This is checked in Phase 10's tests.
9. **Billing maths is pure and tested.** All fee/unit/route/split logic lives in `src/domain/billing/` as pure functions with Vitest tests. UI only formats results.
10. **RFP vocabulary, RFP colours.** Domain terms exactly as the RFP uses them. List-status colour legend is defined once in `src/theme/statusColours.ts` (modernised palette, 1:1 with the legacy legend: private, public, pre-op assessment, holiday, unavailable, free) and used by all three apps.
    **Amended 2026-10-09 (catch-up Phase 29):** the six colours are the palette (`STATUS_PALETTE`, six Design Language tokens, defined once); the availability statuses are a user-maintained master (`masters.slotStatuses`) that picks a token and treatment, and the List types map to their own tokens. The legend is built from the List types plus the active statuses, in all three apps.
    **Amended 2026-10-02 (catch-up Phase 15):** domain terms follow the requirements catalogue, which supersedes the RFP: Booking (not Card) in identifiers and copy, Lists reassigned or moved (never swapped), no "timesheet". Earlier conventions that say Card (6, 7) now read Booking. See the Decisions log.
11. **Ease of use wins arguments.** When choosing between fidelity to the legacy screenshot and a simpler modern pattern, choose simpler — but keep the information architecture recognisable.
12. **Phone frame is the only mobile emulation.** The mobile app renders in the fixed phone frame component on a grey backdrop; never rely on browser viewport size. Web/admin apps are desktop layouts.
    **Amended 2026-07-30 (the PWA target).** The mobile app now runs under *two* hosts: `PhoneFrame` (unchanged, still the prototype's only emulation) and `MobileViewport` (`src/pwa/`, the installed PWA on a real handset). "Never rely on browser viewport size" survives as "never rely on it *directly*": neither the screens nor the shared surfaces read the viewport or `env()` themselves. They read four `--aa-inset-*` custom properties that whichever host is mounting supplies, so one layout serves both. See the inset contract in `src/theme/global.css`, the `host` prop on `MobileApp`, and `aa-prototype/README.md`. The framed pixels are unchanged and locked by `visual/mobile-insets.spec.ts`. Web/admin remain desktop layouts.
13. **Demo-only surfaces are visibly demo-only.** Xero sim, integration simulator, billing monitor internals, the control panel, the harness bar's "Demo actions" menu and the PWA's Demo chip and sheet carry a demo badge ("demo simulation" / "Demo trigger") so demo audiences don't mistake them for proposed product UI. (The billing monitor itself IS proposed product UI — badge only its simulation triggers.) Tooling the catalogue marks Future is badged "Future scope" (`DemoBadge tone="future"`).
14. **Every phase ends the same way:** run `npm run build` + `npx vitest run` green, run the phase's manual test checklist, run the adversarial review-and-fix pass (convention 18, from Phase 05 on), update this file (status row + phase entry + any decisions), and leave the app runnable with `npm run dev`.
15. **Don't gold-plate ahead.** Build only what the current phase's doc lists; later phases depend on the seams described in their docs, not on speculative extras.
16. **Mobile is mobile-first, not a web app in a phone shell.** Inside the phone frame: bottom sheets and slide-in cards, never centred desktop modals; bottom tab bar (Lists · Availability · Balances · More); thumb-reachable and sticky contextual actions; steppers/chips/segmented controls over dropdowns and free text. Micro-delight lives in action feedback (complete-tick, fee value ticking up, submit settling) and never delays a task. The two web apps are proper desktop layouts (hover states, keyboard-friendly tables).
17. **The `docs/design/` mockups are the authoritative visual reference.** `Design Language.dc.html` is the token source of truth — palette, neutrals, the six status colours (with tint/on-tint values and the hatched Unavailable / dashed Free treatments), type (Schibsted Grotesk UI + Spline Sans Mono data with tabular-nums), 4pt spacing, radii (ctl 10 / card 14 / panel 20 / sheet 24-top / pill 999), elevations e-0…e-3, scrim rgba(23,35,32,0.32), and the six named motion patterns (control-press, selection-slide, sheet-in 320/260ms, card-advance 260/240ms with −24% parallax, complete-tick, value-tick; reduced-motion → 80ms fades; corrected from "four" in UI unification U1, question 27). The six sample pages are the layout reference for their screens; each phase doc names its pages. Two hard rules: (a) AA crimson #A91E3E is identity only — masthead, active nav, avatars — never buttons, never status; deep teal #0D6E63 is the only action colour. (b) **Where a mockup simplified a business rule for demo purposes, the RFP rule wins** — see the Decisions log entries below. Extend the design's patterns to screens it doesn't cover; don't invent a second visual language.
18. **Adversarial review-and-fix pass after every build phase (Phase 05 onward).** Once a phase's work items are built and its manual test checklist + `npm run build`/`npx vitest run` are green — and *before* writing the PROGRESS entry — run an independent adversarial review of the phase's work, then fix what it finds:
    - **(a) Fan out a few (≈3) independent Opus review subagents in parallel** (the Agent tool), one per lens: **quality** (code quality, reuse/simplification, adherence to these conventions and the design tokens — crimson-is-identity / teal-only actions, the no-en/em-dash app-copy rule, mobile-first sheet patterns, the `mutate()`-only write discipline — and no gold-plating ahead of the plan); **bugs/correctness** (logic errors, guard/lifecycle correctness, edge cases, seed/clock determinism + domain purity, audit completeness, fee/route maths); and **plan adherence** (every work item, checklist item and cited requirement actually delivered; scope fences respected; Decisions-log rulings honoured). Each reviewer reads PROGRESS.md + the phase doc + the requirements it cites + the relevant `docs/rfp-reference/` sources, then reviews the actual phase diff and returns ranked findings with `file:line` and a concrete failure scenario. Scale the fan-out up (more agents / finer lenses) for the load-bearing money and integration phases (08 to 11), and treat Phase 12's pass as a whole-prototype QA sweep, not just its own diff.
    - **(b) The orchestrator (this phase's session) independently verifies each finding** against the source docs and the actual code before touching anything — the `REVIEW-KICKOFF-PROMPT.md` discipline: never fix on a paraphrase, never blindly defer, and never re-raise anything already settled in the Decisions log. Dedupe, then fix the confirmed findings (adding a test wherever a bug had none).
    - **(c) Re-green** `npm run build` + `npx vitest run`, then record the pass in the PROGRESS phase entry — findings confirmed/fixed, anything deliberately *not* treated as a defect (with the why), and tests added — in the style of the 2026-07-23 Phase 01/02 review-fix entry. (That entry was this loop piloted retroactively on Phases 01/02; it is a standing step from Phase 05 on.) From 16 November 2026 (the `run-build-phase` skill) the reviewers run in the background beside the screenshot and demo-guide work, and re-greening is the full `phase-check.mjs` run.

19. **Catalogue screenshots match the app after every catch-up phase (Phase 14 onward).** The phase creates or updates the capture recipes (`requirements-board/capture/recipes/`) for every item it covers and every recipe its changes broke, captures those recipes alone (`phase-check.mjs --capture <IDs>`: a dry run of just them, then their capture; never a full dry run, which takes as long as a full capture), checks the new shots by eye, keeps `capture/ATLAS.md` current, then runs one full capture (`--capture all`) in the background at the very end with no failed recipe, and finishes with `npm run verify:board` green. From 16 November 2026 this runs beside the review pass rather than after it. The step is spelled out under "Catalogue screenshots" in `catch-up/ROADMAP.md`; record the REPORT.md counts in the phase entry.
20. **A check that should alert, not stop, is a warning rule (catch-up Phase 15a).** It is a rule in `src/domain/warnings/rules/` (registered in `WARNING_RULES`, its id in `WarningRuleId`, its facts from `store/warnings.ts`'s `warningFactsFor`, its parameters in `appSettings`) with a sample in `src/store/warningSamples.ts`. It never becomes a blocker in `lifecycle.ts`, a confirm step at submit or a tap-to-read popover: the shared triangle, the Booking's warnings panel, the Day view outline and the To-do card show it with no UI change.

## Decisions log

Record every deviation from a phase doc, every resolved ambiguity, and every killed idea, with a
one-line why. Later sessions must not re-litigate entries here.

- **2026-11-11 · The modifier master is the NZSA RVG 2021 table as printed, plus AA's own; codes are not keys** (catch-up Phase 19b; US-05.1.5, RV-38). Generated from the catalogue's AR-34 files (`npm run rvg:modifiers` writes `seed/rvgModifiers.generated.ts`; a Vitest drift guard re-parses the files), 30 rows, values as printed, a value that is not a plain whole number entered at capture within the printed bounds ("2 [Max]" at most 2, "4-6" 4 to 6, "2 + Time" at least 2), hidden ids `MOD-RVG-<code>`, en and em dashes normalised. **SUPERSEDES** the 2026-07-22 "table lives in `modifierCodes.ts`, values demo-plausible" entry and its PO1 and PO2 list.
- **2026-11-11 · No ASA seed: the ASA grade is one optional modifier with an explanation** (catch-up Phase 19b; RV-22, US-03.3.4, US-05.1.5, OQ-95 part 2). **SUPERSEDES** the 2026-07-22 "ASA seeding values" ruling. Seeded AS1 and AS2 claim nothing (ASA I or II is AS1 at 0), AS3 and AS4 claim their code with a seeded explanation; the generator still draws `asaDraw`.
- **2026-11-11 · P1 is included, pre-applied at 0 and removable, on the 20 Neurosurgery and Spine codes, on the RVG group** (catch-up Phase 19b; RV-09, US-05.1.4, D43 superseded in part 20 October). From the CSV, `RvgGroup.includedModifierIds`; hip and shoulder rows include nothing (P1 an ordinary claim there). **SUPERSEDES** the absorbed-P1 ruling (refusal, strike-through, "Includes positioning", Phase 19's interim `includesModifierCodes`) and the 2026-10-02 "default modifiers, pre-filled and untickable" reading.
- **2026-11-11 · Ellison's A1 is the pre-applied, removable age modifier** (catch-up Phase 19b; US-03.3.8). The 2026-07-23 A1 relabel now stands as the age rule (72 on 21 Jul 2026); her claim is gone and her fee is unchanged ($344.50, 13 units).
- **2026-11-11 · No stacking limit; the age band is pre-applied, its boundaries D29's default** (catch-up Phase 19b; OQ-95 part 2 answered, part 1 open). Completed years on the List's date, lower bounds inclusive (0 A2, 1 A1, 2 to 69 none, 70 to 79 A1, 80 and over A2), none on H6b and P2 (every row carrying those codes, AA's own P2 too), in `AGE_BANDS` in `domain/billing/modifiers.ts`; provisional only on the Admin Modifiers tab. **SUPERSEDES** the 2026-07-27 one-per-band reading (and PA5 stacking).
- **2026-11-11 · The itemised Modifiers ledger and the picker with an inline explanation** (catch-up Phase 19b; US-03.3.4). **SUPERSEDES** the 2026-07-28 modifier picker shape (segmented bands plus "Also applies" chips).
- **2026-11-11 · Modifiers are itemised records; nothing is locked** (catch-up Phase 19b; DM-44). Claims stored (`modifierClaims`, each with an explanation of at most 200 characters, units only where the printed value is not a plain number); age and included modifiers derived, removals stored (`removedModifierIds`, audited, Put back); one function returns the itemised list and the M total = 19a's starting modifier units + the list; never counted twice (a duplicate claim adds nothing); `editProcedure` cannot write claims; a claim with no explanation is refused at claim time and at completion (US-03.6.1's backstop, finished by Phase 21). The manual M adjustment (`modifierUnitsCaptured` overridden) is kept as an adjustment, never a way to claim a modifier.

- **2026-11-11 · The RVG groups are the one master list; base units sit on the RVG group alone** (catch-up Phase 19; US-05.1.1, US-05.1.3, FT-05.1, DM-13, DM-43; OQ-88 / D39, OQ-62, D12 superseded a second time and extended 5 November; **SUPERSEDES** the flat `RvgCode` table keyed by its code, `Procedure.rvgBaseCode` and the 2026-07-22 demo-plausible invented five-digit codes for the published rows, RV-41). One module, `domain/billing/rvgGroups.ts` (types re-exported from `types.ts`): `RvgGroup { id, code, description, anatomy, baseUnits, baseUnitsRange?, modifierUnits, retired, includesModifierCodes? (INTERIM, 19b) }`. The id is a unique identifier only, never shown (seed `RG001`…, runtime `RGN001`); the printed code is not unique (two T2s, two P6s as published, plus AA rows that carry the nearest printed code with AA's own description and figure). `Procedure.rvgGroupId` is optional and the Procedure's `description` stays the text received. A Contract states no base units (19a may only name a default RVG code, which fills an empty one through `pickRvgGroup`). No procedure list, general procedure, body-section picker or tabs.
- **2026-11-11 · RV-10 under D3: any base-unit value is accepted; an out-of-range one warns, mild, after the procedure** (catch-up Phase 19; OQ-56, OQ-101 / D35; **SUPERSEDES** the Phase 04 stepper clamp and the in-range completion rule "needs a selected unit value between"). One answer, `baseUnitsFor`: a typed override, else the chosen value on a ranged row, else the row's starting figure (the range's lower bound), else 0 with no RVG code. A ranged row starts at its figure, so nothing is left unchosen. `outsideGuide` (the recorded value differs from the starting value and lies outside the range, or off the figure) drives one `baseUnitsOutsideGuide` warning per Procedure, strength mild (a picked reading: OQ-56 sets none), skipped on an additional procedure (its base units are not charged). The store accepts any whole value of 0 or more ("Base units must be a whole number."); nothing blocks.
- **2026-11-11 · The capture picker is a type-ahead on code and description, and the RVG code is optional** (catch-up Phase 19; US-05.1.1, US-03.3.1; **SUPERSEDES** the Phase 04 picker grouped by anatomical site). `CodePickerSheet` (name kept) is one flat list: code, description, a neutral anatomy label and "B 6" or "B 10 to 12"; "H1" lists every H1 row; a short default list leads with the current row. "Change" or "Choose" and "Clear" on the "RVG code" card (hook `capture-procedure-code` kept by an explicit `shot` on `CaptureSection`). The validator no longer demands an RVG code or a billing line: a Procedure with neither completes at $0 (zero-charge rules are Phase 21's).
- **2026-11-11 · The NZSA RVG 2021 groups replace the invented five-digit codes; seeded Procedures keep their fees through AA rows** (catch-up Phase 19; RV-41; AR-16, AR-34, AR-35). A published row is used for a legacy code only where its base units equal the legacy figure and its examples fit (8 codes); otherwise AA's own row (20). The generator keeps drawing from the legacy ranges through the seed-only bridge, so the RNG sequence and every generated Booking are unchanged (proved by a full-state diff against HEAD in the review). The HL7 fixtures' display codes now read the printed codes (A3, LL1…).
- **2026-11-11 · 2026-10-02 readings superseded** (catch-up Phase 19): "default modifiers pre-filled and untickable" (modifiers are 19b's: only age and included modifiers are pre-applied, none locked) and AA groups as many-to-many tags across groups (US-05.1.3: the anatomy heading is a label; AA's own rows sit beside the published ones).
- **2026-11-11 · Specialties and funding tags are masters; a surgeon holds one or more specialties** (catch-up Phase 18a; US-13.4.4, US-13.4.5, US-13.6.6, DM-63, DM-64; D3, D4; **SUPERSEDES** the free-text `Surgeon.specialty`). `masters.specialties` (`SPC-…`, runtime `SPN###`) and `masters.fundingTags` (`TAG-…`, runtime `TGN###`, `order` is step-rail order, optional `funderPartyId`). `Surgeon.specialtyIds` is required in the store (`cleanSpecialtyIds`: `specialtyRequired`, `specialtyUnknown`); every screen shows it through `surgeonSpecialtyLabel`. "Office assigns a Draft List to me" assigns the soonest fitting request in the persona's open sessions, skipping a not-preferred pairing through a boolean (no preference revealed); with none, it logs a request for her next open session and assigns that. PWA only, badged.
- **2026-10-10 · Admin Day rail order** (catch-up Phase 31; FT-13.7). Calendar, To-do (15a), Draft Lists, then Phase 32's pool, notes, Awaiting review.
- **2026-10-10 · Prepayment on a Draft List waits for its first assignment** (catch-up Phase 31; US-06.3.5, D20; built default with 27 unbuilt). A Booking on a Draft List has no billing context, so no prepayment invoice or warning; `assignDraftList` returns `firstAssignmentBookingIds` (Bookings that never had an anaesthetist) as 27's seam and runs nothing; re-dating, detaching and reassigning a returned List re-trigger nothing.

- **2026-10-09 · Conflicts are derived from facts and reconciled inside `mutate()`** (catch-up Phase 30; US-01.5.2, US-01.5.4; SUPERSEDES the per-path stamping of 2026-07-23 "Availability reconciliation, both directions", Phase 06 decision (1)'s seeding, Phase 29's `availabilityClash` and Phase 28's `closedHospitalConflict` stamp in `placeListOnSlot`). `ListConflict` holds a cause (`holiday:<id>` or `availability:<slotId>:<statusKey>`) and references, never a message; `describeConflict` words it from the current records, so a renamed holiday or status changes every line with no write. `store/conflictReconcile.ts`, called only from `mutate()`, re-runs the one rule over every List whose facts the patch touched (changed Lists, Lists in changed Slots, Lists at the old and new date and hospital of a changed holiday, every List when the status master changes, and Lists the patch removed) and appends `list.conflict` / `list.conflictResolved` metas to the same commit, from fact-level diffs (a List locking or an office clear writes none). `mutate()` returns `MutationResult { conflictsRaised, conflictsResolved }`. No store action writes `List.conflicts`; the seed ends with `reconcileAllConflicts`.
- **2026-10-09 · A conflicted List changes colour** (catch-up Phase 30; US-01.5.2 "the List changes colour"; AMENDS Phase 06 decision (1), border and badge only). The block takes `semantic.warning` tint and a 1.5px warning border, keeps the kind's left bar and the hospital line, and its second line becomes the reason ("Hospital closed", "Anaesthetist unavailable"). A block needing attention only for a missing surgeon keeps its status tint. No new hex. The legend's "Conflict" chip is the legend entry and the focus filter in one, as "Needs attention" already is.
- **2026-10-09 · "Booked List" means any assigned List** (catch-up Phase 30; US-01.5.2 AC2, US-01.5.4 AC1). A List exists only once assigned, and a recurring booking creates its List before any Bookings, so an empty assigned List conflicts too; the Conflicts screen shows the Booking count. AUTHORISED and backdrop Lists never conflict; a List with no Slot record can carry only a holiday conflict.
- **2026-10-09 · An office clear holds only while its cause stands** (catch-up Phase 30; OQ-09 answered, plain soft warning). `clearListConflict` records a `ConflictClear` (no reason required, an optional note) and the reconcile holds the conflict back; when the cause goes the clear is dropped, so a clash that comes back flags again. "Flag again" (`restoreListConflict`) removes the clear.
- **2026-10-09 · Assigning, phone-booking or moving onto a closed session is accepted and flagged** (catch-up Phase 30; OQ-09, US-01.5.2 AC1 and AC3; SUPERSEDES Phase 28's interim `slotNotAvailable` refusal and the closed-target half of `moveListToSlot`'s `targetNotOpen`; an occupied target is still refused). Inline warnings show before confirm in Assign List, phone advice, Edit list and Reassign, and on each Move Booking candidate (a tap there moves at once), and never disable the confirm. Hospital selects read "Southern Cross · closed".
- **2026-10-09 · Reassigning from a closed session keeps its status by default** (catch-up Phase 30). "Vacated session becomes" defaults to "Keep as is" (the sick anaesthetist stays unavailable); from an open session it is still Free (OQ-84's recommendation). The picker keeps 17's grouping and adds a collapsed "Not available" group of empty closed sessions (accept and flag).
- **2026-10-09 · The Wed 22 seeded conflicts are real facts** (catch-up Phase 30; replaces `applyPhase06Conflicts`). Dr Rutherford's Wed 22 AM is Unavailable, "Unwell, short notice", recorded by the office (a Kirsty audit row at 07:40); his List (no Bookings in the seed) stays and is flagged. Southern Cross is closed on Wed 22 (`HH900`, "Theatre maintenance closure"), which flags its four Lists that day: Morrison PM, Ngata PM, Sharma PM and Hughes AM. Seeded conflicts are stamped at the seed clock (08:00).
- **2026-10-09 · Permanent Lists are renamed recurring bookings** (catch-up Phase 30; DM-53, US-01.3.2). In model, code and copy: `RecurringBooking`, `masters.recurringBookings`, `?view=recurringBookings`, the actions and audit codes (`recurringBooking.*`), the generator's "template" wording. A recurring booking is the standing intersection of hospital, anaesthetist and surgeon on a day and session, a pattern of Lists, not a patient Booking; copy never shortens it to "booking". Seed ids `RCB###` and runtime `RCBN###`, because `RB` is Phase 16's BCTI-history namespace (`L-RB-`, `RBINV`). Null hospital or surgeon kept as is (Phase 31's pairing rule).
- **2026-10-09 · Recurring bookings create their Lists across the horizon, after the calendar, and changes reach the canvas through "Apply to canvas now"** (catch-up Phase 30; US-01.3.2, OQ-81 part 1; SUPERSEDES Phase 07's store behaviour, "master edits apply only to future generated days"). The pure `domain/recurringBookingProjection.ts` plans create, update, remove, kept and skipped from tomorrow to the far end of the horizon setting; add, edit and retire apply their plan in one `mutate()`, and the sheet's primary "Apply to canvas now" saves and projects at once, with a live preview from the same plan. Created Lists are ACTIVE, empty and carry `recurringBookingId`; an office edit (hospital, surgeon, notes, times) or move drops it, and a moved List keeps `recurringOrigin` so its old session is never painted again. Kept: Lists with Bookings (cancelled ones count, as for Phase 28's horizon shortening), with notes, attachments or clears, SUBMITTED or AUTHORISED, office-edited or moved, or from another recurring booking. Removals are only of its own empty ACTIVE Lists. A session already closed is skipped and counted ("not painted", Phase 31's Draft List). The view-level "Apply to canvas now" re-paints sessions that have come free and never removes. Weekend patterns, start and end dates and retire (no hard delete; removals only) work; the generator uses `activeOn` and agrees with the projection (a fresh seed plans nothing to create, update or remove).
- **2026-10-09 · Hospital holidays can be edited and deleted** (catch-up Phase 30; US-01.5.1, FT-01.5). The hospital of a holiday row is fixed (moving a closure to another hospital is delete and add); editing or deleting resolves its flags through the reconcile, and a calendar view shows each hospital's month.
- **2026-10-09 · What a conflict is follows the catalogue at `60e2d1e` (unchanged since `3d3a18c`)** (catch-up Phase 30; US-01.5.2, US-01.5.4, OQ-64, OQ-81). A List at a closed hospital, or a List in a session already marked unavailable. A recurring booking on an unavailable session is not a conflict: it is skipped (Phase 31 makes it a Draft List). An anaesthetist marking a booked session unavailable is return-or-assign (Phase 32, US-01.5.5); until then it is flagged as a named interim, through the shared per-session write `applySessionWrites`, the one place 32 hooks in. A sickness the office records (the anaesthetist phones in) keeps the List and its Bookings and is a conflict: provisional (OQ-81 part 3), on `simulate-sickness` and the seeded Rutherford Wed 22 AM.

- **2026-10-09 · The Slot status set is a user-maintained master list** (catch-up Phase 29; OQ-64 answered, US-01.2.2, US-01.2.1; AMENDS convention 10; SUPERSEDES 2026-07-21 "Status colour mapping" as a closed six-key set). `masters.slotStatuses` holds `SlotStatus` records, availability values only: a fixed internal ID that rules read (`SlotStatusKey`), an editable label, long label, description, colour (one of the six Design Language tokens, never a free hex) and treatment, "open for bookings", "anaesthetists can set", one default. The palette stays in `src/theme/statusColours.ts` as `STATUS_PALETTE` (same hexes) with `resolveStatusVisual`; the List types (private, public, pre-op) are a fixed List attribute mapped to their own tokens (`LIST_KIND_VISUAL`, `LIST_KIND_LABELS`; the OQ-17 answer). The master never holds a List state (DRAFT, ACTIVE, SUBMITTED, AUTHORISED; US-01.2.2 since 2026-10-07): `validateSlotStatusDraft` refuses those names, "Draft" and "Draft List" as labels, and the table says "In use" or "Retired", never "Active".
- **2026-10-09 · One mechanism, with series** (catch-up Phase 29; OQ-27 and OQ-64 answered, US-01.5.3; SUPERSEDES item (2) of the 2026-07-22 external plan review, availability written to a master). The calendar (mobile and web) writes the Slot's own status. A series (`schedule.availabilitySeries`, `AS####`) is a rule (weekdays, AM, PM or both, every 1 to 4 weeks, start, optional until) plus exceptions; it writes its Slots (`Slot.seriesId` is a pointer only), and a single-instance edit or delete is stored as an exception so no later series write, roll forward or horizon extend overwrites it. Nothing reads availability from anywhere but Slots.
- **2026-10-09 · The series fill rule, on every generating path** (catch-up Phase 29; OQ-81 part 1). A series fills only sessions at the default status and in no other series, and reports the rest as "left as it is". One helper, `seriesCalendarFor`, feeds active series into `generateCanvasForDates` through `canvasMastersFrom(state, dates)` on every generating path (roll forward, horizon extend, a new or reactivated anaesthetist, an earlier start date), painted with the calendar after the seed's leave and BEFORE recurring bookings, so a recurring booking on a series-closed session is traced as 28's `RecurringClash` (Phase 31's Draft List), never placed. The generator's closed test is `isClosed` over the status records (an admin-added closed status stops a recurring booking too). Deleting a series ends it from today: its untouched future instances return to the default, an edited one keeps its status as a one-off, past ones stay.
- **2026-10-09 · A bookable status over a List raises nothing and clears its availability flag** **SUPERSEDED 2026-10-09 (catch-up Phase 30):** conflicts are derived from facts and reconciled inside `mutate()`; a bookable status resolves the availability conflict through that one rule, with no per-path clear. (catch-up Phase 29; SUPERSEDES 2026-07-23 "Availability reconciliation, both directions" for the un-block direction; the restatus half went in Phase 28).
- **2026-10-09 · The clash with a List is a flag, in one function** **SUPERSEDED 2026-10-09 (catch-up Phase 30):** `availabilityClash` is gone; the one rule is `domain/conflicts.ts`, reconciled in `mutate()`, and the shared per-session write `applySessionWrites` writes Slots only (it stays the one place Phase 32 hooks return-or-assign in). (catch-up Phase 29; US-01.5.5, US-01.5.3). `availabilityClash(list, status)` decides every case: a closed status over a List flags it once (replacing, never stacking), naming who marked it ("Dr Souter marked this session Unavailable. The List is still in place; reassign it if it needs cover."); a bookable status clears it; the List's surgeon, hospital, Bookings, times and kind are never touched. `'flag'` is the INTERIM for Phase 32's return-or-assign when an anaesthetist marks a booked session closed (one-off, range, series or instance edit); generation never reaches it (31's Draft List takes the traced clashes). No line anywhere says the office was notified; the interim says the List is flagged on the office's Day view.
- **2026-10-09 · Statuses are retired, never deleted; IDs are fixed** (catch-up Phase 29). Seeded IDs `free`, `holiday`, `unavailable` (Phase 28's stored values, so no Slot was rewritten); an added status gets `ST####`; IDs are never edited and can never equal a List kind. Exactly one default, bookable; the default and a status an active series uses cannot be retired (the refusal names the count); a retired status leaves the choices and legends and still renders on the sessions that carry it; restore brings it back. Making another status the default moves the default.
- **2026-10-09 · One display key space** (catch-up Phase 29). `displayStatusKey` returns the List's kind when a List is in the Slot, otherwise the Slot's status ID unchanged, typed `DisplayKey = ListKind | SlotStatusKey`; 28's closed `DisplayStatusKey` and `SLOT_STATUSES` are gone, `SlotStatus` now names the master record. `isOpenSlot(slot, list, statuses)` (no List and open for bookings) lives in `domain/slotStatus.ts` with `displayStatusLabel(key, statuses)`; `SlotView` carries `open`.
- **2026-10-09 · No "available for emergency" and no extra kind of unavailable is seeded** (catch-up Phase 29; the owner's starting set). The seed is Free (default, dashed), Holiday (long label "On holiday") and Unavailable (hatched); an admin adds more (Greg's "several versions of unavailable ... same effect").
- **2026-10-09 · One availability store** (catch-up Phase 29). `masters.availability` was already gone (Phase 28); `masters.listStatuses` became `masters.slotStatuses`. Availability lives on Slots alone; series are rules that write Slots.
- **2026-10-09 · "Slot" never reaches app copy, codes included** (catch-up Phase 29; OQ-64 part 5). The master is "Availability statuses" (`?view=availability-statuses`; the old `listStatuses` value still opens it); audit codes say `availability.*` and `availabilityStatus.*` (the Audit viewer prints raw codes); the validator refuses "slot" and en or em dashes in admin-entered labels.
- **2026-10-09 · Legend order and the anaesthetist's choices** (catch-up Phase 29). The legend lists the List types, then the active statuses with the default (Free) last, as the Design Language legend does (Admin Day Tue 21 is pixel-identical to Phase 28); the anaesthetist's choices list Free, On holiday, Unavailable in `order`.
- **2026-10-09 · Availability is a status on the Slot, the one mechanism** (catch-up Phase 28; OQ-17, OQ-27, OQ-64 answered, FT-01.2, DM-04; SUPERSEDES 2026-07-23 "Availability reconciliation, both directions"). `setAvailability` writes `Slot.status` and `Slot.note` and nothing else; there is no availability master and nothing is restatused or reconciled. A Slot holding a List keeps the List's kind and the List gets one availability conflict (replace, never stack) when marked unavailable or holiday: **interim until Phase 32** offers return to the office or assign to a colleague (US-01.5.5). Marking it free writes no conflict (the old "Marked available, but this List carries booking context" conflict is gone); an earlier conflict stays until Phase 30 adds clearing.
- **2026-10-09 · Reassign moves the List between Slots** (catch-up Phase 28; US-01.4.1; SUPERSEDES the 4th review #6 and Phase 06 free-target, absorb, regenerate mechanism with default Unavailable). The List keeps its id, Bookings, notes, attachments and history; `slotId` and the denormalised fields change; availability conflicts drop, holiday conflicts stay; the Slot's own times travel. **The vacated session returns to Free by default, with Unavailable or Holiday on request: OQ-84's recommendation, PROVISIONAL until OQ-84 is answered (this entry is its one place).** No List is absorbed, created or deleted; `list.absorb` and `list.regenerate` are no longer written.
- **2026-10-09 · One displayed status** (catch-up Phase 28; US-01.2.3, US-01.4.2; SUPERSEDES Phase 06 decision (5)). One pure `displayStatusKey(slot, list)` (`domain/slots.ts`): the List's kind when a List is in the Slot, the Slot's status otherwise; it takes no Bookings. All three apps and every finder read it through the Slot views; "free" for a finder is `isOpenSlot` (free and no List). Handoff P5 is closed. Convention 10 (six statuses, all three apps) stands; the key is now derived.
- **2026-10-09 · Generation draws nothing** (catch-up Phase 28; US-01.1.1, OQ-81 part 1 settled in the room; SUPERSEDES "Slot-hashed generator randomness" as a generation rule). `generateCanvasForDates` writes every Slot free, paints the calendar, then the recurring bookings (weekday guard kept until Phase 30); a recurring booking under leave projects nothing and is returned as a clash (18 in the seed, pinned; Phase 31 makes them Draft Lists). The slot RNG survives only for the seed's recorded window (`seedRecordedWindow`, 2026-07-07 to 2026-08-16, the same per-slot draws as before) and the filler Bookings.
- **2026-10-09 · The horizon is a setting** (catch-up Phase 28; FT-01.1; SUPERSEDES the fixed `HORIZON_FUTURE_MONTHS`). `appSettings.schedule.horizonMonths`, 4 by default, 1 to 24; every reader goes through `horizonFor(today, months)` / `scheduleHorizon`. Extending generates the new days exactly as a roll-forward; shortening drops far-edge Slots and their empty Lists (ids audited) and is refused while a List there holds a Booking (cancelled ones count, so none is orphaned) or an attachment. The same value is no change.
- **2026-10-09 · Ids** (catch-up Phase 28; AMENDS "Deterministic IDs"). Slots `S-<reg>-<date>-<session>`; projected and seeded Lists keep `L-<reg>-<date>-<session>` (the session they were born in, never parsed); runtime Lists `LG####`. The Phase 02 note "always resolve slots via `listForSlot`" is replaced by `slotFor` + `listInSlot`.
- **2026-10-09 · Every Slot is stored; "slot" never reaches the UI** (catch-up Phase 28; OQ-64 answered). The Slot statuses start as free, unavailable and holiday behind one label lookup, `displayStatusLabel` (Phase 29 makes them a user-maintained list); the List kinds private, public and pre-op stay a List attribute outside the catalogue's model, so the six-colour design language holds. The UI, audit labels and field labels say session; the audit codes a Slot writes are `session.status`, `session.times` and `session.coverRequest` (entity type `session`), because the Audit viewer prints raw codes beside the labels (a deviation from the phase doc's `slot.*` names). The legacy labels `list.absorb`, `list.restatus`, `list.regenerate` and `list.coverRequest` were removed (the repo's label-honesty test; the persist bump reseeds any older history). Field label `status` stays "Status" (a key shared with other entities).
- **2026-10-09 · One schedule-settings record; times on the Slot** (catch-up Phase 28; US-01.1.4). `appSettings.schedule` holds the horizon and the default AM and PM times; per-Slot overrides live on the Slot and travel with a reassigned List; a session keeps its default shape on the grid with one Booking. The four hard-coded duplicates are gone; "Use default" clears an override, and an override is written only where a time differs from the default.
- **2026-10-09 · An empty session carries no List state** (catch-up Phase 28; EP-07). Every List created by assignment, projection, the addendum or the PWA stand-in is `ACTIVE`; `DRAFT` and "Draft List" stay reserved for Phase 31.
- **2026-10-09 · Interim rulings** **AMENDED 2026-10-09 (catch-up Phase 30):** assignment, phone advice and a move onto an unavailable or holiday session are now accepted and flagged (`slotNotAvailable` and the closed-target half of `targetNotOpen` are gone). (catch-up Phase 28). Assignment onto an unavailable or holiday session is refused until Phase 30 (accept and flag); the post-op addendum creates its own List in today's open session (copying the original's hospital, surgeon and kind, clearing any cover marker) until Phase 38b; a hospital message whose target session holds no List parks for the office (`noTargetList`) until Phase 33; a recurring booking on an unavailable Slot is traced, not projected, until Phase 31.
- **2026-10-09 · Denormalised List fields** (catch-up Phase 28). A List keeps `anaesthetistId`, `dateISO` and `session` as copies of its Slot's, written only by the actions that set `slotId`, checked by the seed invariant test (and fuzzed in review).
- **2026-10-09 · Start date and active gate the Slots** (catch-up Phase 28; US-01.1.3, FT-01.1). `Anaesthetist.startDateISO` is required; Slots exist from the start date and only while active. A start-date or active edit adds or removes Slots **from today on only** and never deletes a List (refused `listsBeforeStart` or `listsAhead`). Reading: a start date moved later than a past day leaves that past day's Slots as history (dates before today are never touched).
- **2026-10-09 · The office availability finder** (catch-up Phase 28; US-01.4.2, US-01.3.5, US-01.3.6). "Find available" in the Admin Day header lists the open sessions for a day and session through 17's `AnaesthetistCandidates` only (tier order, shuffled within a tier from `<date>:<session>:<suggestionSeq>`, the tier filter, not-preferred pairings apart once a surgeon is chosen); picking opens Assign List with the surgeon chosen. The anaesthetists' finders stay name-ordered and untiered. The pairing acknowledgement is written by the office entry points (`assignListToSlot`, `reassignList`), never by `moveListToSlot`, so the anaesthetist's own moves (Phases 32, 32a) log none.
- **2026-10-09 · A move recalculates nothing** (catch-up Phase 28; US-06.3.5, US-06.5.4, D20 superseded). `moveListToSlot` touches no invoice, prepayment or billing case (test: deep-equal before and after); none was found to remove. It carries the seam comment for Phase 41's payee repoint (OQ-80, D38).
- **2026-10-09 · Seed: the recorded window and one artefact fixed** (catch-up Phase 28). The golden test reproduces the demo window (1,148 sessions), all 172 Bookings and the 17 `SEED_LIST_IDS` exactly; the far edge (last seven days) was regenerated once (free 119 to 144, private 51 to 36, public 15 to 12, unavailable 7 to 0, pre-op 4); Phase 17's canvas fingerprint was re-pinned. Souter's Fri 24 Lists no longer carry the leave note "Annual leave / back Monday" (an artefact of painting a List over a leave row; she works those sessions, so the Slot is free).
- **2026-10-09 · One room per surgeon** (catch-up Phase 17; US-13.6.1, DM-32). `Surgeon.roomId` is required and a room's surgeons are derived from it, never stored on the room, so membership has one source and is changed from the surgeon. One contact email and phone per room; several rooms or contacts per surgeon is Phase 42's if AA asks.
- **2026-10-09 · The HPI CPN is one required `hpiId` on a surgeon, unique across practitioners** (catch-up Phase 17; OQ-52 answered, US-13.6.2). The same field name and label ("HPI CPN") as the anaesthetist's, which stays optional; "HPI id" is relabelled everywhere. Stored through `normaliseHpiCpn`, shape-checked only (two digits then four letters), and refused when held by any surgeon or anaesthetist, whichever record is saved first. Never presented as the patient's NHI. Check characters and register lookup are Phase 40a's.
- **2026-10-09 · Pairing preferences are one private two-way model; not preferred warns and never blocks** (catch-up Phase 17; OQ-43 answered, D44; US-13.6.3, US-13.6.4, US-01.3.5, DM-54). Each entry has `kind` (not preferred or preferred) and `raisedBy` (which side asked), is kept by the office on both the surgeon profile and the Admin anaesthetist record, and lives in the office-only `officePrivate` slice that `officePrivacy.test.ts` keeps out of every mobile, web, PWA, shell, demo and shared surface. A not-preferred pairing on either side wins over a preferred one; it is grouped apart, labelled, selectable and warned on every office path, never refused. Going ahead writes `list.pairingAcknowledged` or `permanentList.pairingAcknowledged` in the same commit, once, only when the pairing changed and only for an office actor (the one new rule; cheap). Preferred is marked only. Nothing is anaesthetist-facing, and an anaesthetist's own hand-on gets no warning (US-01.4.5). A same-side duplicate or contradiction is refused; the other side may be added; ending keeps the record.
- **2026-10-09 · Priority tiers: four, office only, Tier 4 the default with no entry** (catch-up Phase 17; US-01.3.6, D36 pending OQ-102). Held in the office slice keyed by anaesthetist, never on `Anaesthetist`. Candidates are grouped by not preferred first, then ordered by tier within each group, shuffled within a tier by `mulberry32` keyed on the List id and a per-open counter (`shell.suggestionSeq`, zeroed by Reset, so a fresh Reset replays the same orders). Names come from `TIER_LABELS` with a "provisional" line while `TIER_NAMES_PROVISIONAL`.
- **2026-10-09 · Surgeon groups are a new master beside `organisations`** (catch-up Phase 17; US-13.4.1). `SG-COS` Canterbury Orthopaedic Surgeons mirrors the `ORG.cos` organisation by name; `organisations` and the COS Contract are untouched. Phase 18's COS rooms holder links to `SG-COS`.
- **2026-10-09 · The office's Reassign list is "moving a List" for US-01.3.5 and "cover" for US-01.3.6** (catch-up Phase 17). It gets the grouped, tier-ordered picker and the warning; the office's single-Booking move changes no List's pairing and gets none. This phase supersedes no July ruling; it extends the Phase 06 advisory reading (amber, never a hard block).
- **2026-10-09 · The payable is the gross amount; a payment releases exactly what was received** (catch-up Phase 16; FT-10.3, US-10.2.1, RV-07; SUPERSEDES 2026-07-29 "Xero money flow and illustrative AA service fee" and restores the 2026-07-24 `D-payee-amount` outcome as a catalogue rule). Pure `payableReleasedFor` (`domain/billing/payableRelease.ts`); the 5% fee code, fields and copy are gone. The release stays per payment through today's Run payables; the weekly ISO-week payment cycle (US-10.2.7, OQ-47 Proposed) is Phase 39a's.
- **2026-10-09 · AA's fee is a monthly AA-FEE invoice from settings** (catch-up Phase 16; D1, OQ-02 answered). Every active anaesthetist gets one per month (fixed items only when they have no BCTIs; FT-10.3's "each anaesthetist"). Settings live in `appSettings.aaFee` (DM-31), not `DemoSettings`, with every amount ex GST and GST once at the foot of the fee invoice (US-05.2.7, Greg 2026-10-07): no inclusive toggle, so US-10.3.1's $700 is the fee before GST ($805.00 with GST). The seeded schedule ($350 + $150, $5 per BCTI) is a labelled sample until AA's accountant supplies the real one (OQ-60 part 1). A settings change applies from the next run; raised invoices keep their snapshot.
- **2026-10-09 · The BCTI count** (catch-up Phase 16; OQ-60 part 2, OQ-29). One BCTI per receivable invoice (its ACCPAY), counted once against the ACCPAY's stored anaesthetist, only once its receivable is paid in full, in the month it is paid (Greg 2026-10-02, being confirmed with AA's accountant), through `bctisFor` over `bctiRecords` only, with `BCTI_COUNT_RULE.paidOnly` the one switch. Review-pass addition: a BCTI whose paid month was already invoiced (a current month run to date, or a poll catch backdated into an invoiced month) is carried to the next month not yet invoiced, and a charged BCTI never counts again, so no paid BCTI is missed or charged twice. If the accountant counts every issued BCTI, flip `paidOnly`; if "one per procedure" is confirmed, `bctiRecords`, the "Seed a month of BCTIs" action and S3 Beat 4 are re-baselined in one place.
- **2026-10-09 · The fee is never netted and is paid into AA's own account** (catch-up Phase 16; OQ-60 part 3, Greg 2026-10-02 trust law). A rule with no switch: no code path deducts a fee invoice from a payable, a payables run or a disbursement (tested).
- **2026-10-09 · The AA fee invoice is its own case outside `billing.cases`** (catch-up Phase 16; DM-26). Every consumer of `billing.cases` assumes a Booking; FT-10.3 makes the fee distinct from procedure receivables and payables. `billing.aaFeeInvoices` holds it; `XeroAccRec.kind` (`procedure | aaFee`) marks its ACCREC (no ACCPAY); `raiseAnaesthetistInvoiceInto` (over the pure `buildAaFeeInvoice`) is the one path for an invoice from AA to an anaesthetist. Guards: `receivePayment` refuses it, `openAccRecs` and the poll skip it, the payment webhook triggers are hidden on its pair.
- **2026-10-09 · Fee payments are not the anaesthetist's income** (catch-up Phase 16). `recordAaFeePayment` writes a `PaymentIn` (source `aaFee`) and the mirror, never a `BillingReceipt`, so GST activity never sees it.
- **2026-10-09 · No personal information in Xero** (catch-up Phase 16; OQ-30 answered, US-09.3.1). The Appendix 2 reading is confirmed and extended to names: patient and billable-party contacts are named only by `xeroIndividualContactName` ("Patient PT0001", "Billable party BP0001") in the handoff and both seeds; organisation and payee contacts keep their names; the simulator states the confirmed rule instead of a contradiction. Extends 2026-07-28 "Xero invoice pairs are routed" (the patient is named only in the engine-link panel) and keeps 2026-07-22 Fourth review #5.
- **2026-10-09 · The seeded missed webhook is dated July** (catch-up Phase 16 reading). History row `oa02`'s missed payment is dated 2026-07-20 (was its raise date, 24 Jun), so the next-day poll catch lands in July rather than in June, which the seed has already invoiced. Its GST receipt moves from June to July.

- **2026-10-09 · No prepayment completion gate and no override** (catch-up Phase 15a; D5, OQ-57, US-06.3.2 "no block"; SUPERSEDES 2026-07-22 "Second external plan review (Codex)" where pre-payment became a REAL gate, and the gate and override parts of 2026-07-24 "Phase 09 build: decisions"). An unpaid prepayment is a strong before-procedure warning (`prepaymentUnpaid`); completing, submitting, authorising and billing all go through. The mirror-based paid state stays.
- **2026-10-09 · Warnings are derived by one pure routine; only clearances are stored** (catch-up Phase 15a; DM-31). `evaluateWarnings` recomputes every Booking's warnings from facts; an office clearance lives in `schedule.warningClearances`, keyed by warning, outside the Booking, so clearing never touches a locked Booking or its `lastModifiedBy`. A clearance holds only while the finding's strength is no higher than the cleared one: a cleared mild warning that turns strong re-opens.
- **2026-10-09 · Rule parameters live in `appSettings`, not `DemoSettings`; no settings page** (catch-up Phase 15a; US-13.7.4 Future, Greg 2026-10-02 "set it up as a constant").
- **2026-10-09 · No confirm step and no tap-to-read** (catch-up Phase 15a; US-13.7.3, Confirmed 2026-10-02). The triangle is a marker (`span role="img"`), the warning shows at the top of the Booking on opening, and the usual "Submit this list to the office?" sheet is unchanged: it pre-dates warnings and is not the confirm step the room removed.
- **2026-10-09 · The to-do list holds warnings that need action only** (catch-up Phase 15a; FT-13.7). Notices that need none (a List move, the not-preferred pairing notice) go to the shared notification pool Phase 32 builds; the To-do card sits under the mini calendar and Phase 31's Draft Lists and Phase 32's pool stack below it.
- **2026-10-09 · Sample warnings are staged only by the demo actions, and unstaged only while still theirs** (catch-up Phase 15a review). A sample counts as staged only when the demo actions made the last audited change to it, so a real edit to the same values is never reverted; unstaging is refused once a real pre-procedure invoice was raised on the sample (Reset clears it); unstaging restores the seed's last-modified stamp when nobody else has touched the Booking since.

- **2026-10-02 · Booking replaces Card everywhere; Lists are reassigned or moved, never swapped; no "timesheet"** (catch-up Phase 15; amends convention 10). The catalogue's vocabulary supersedes the RFP's, in identifiers as well as copy (beyond RV-12's "identifiers may stay", because later phases write new Booking code). "Card" means only the physical hospital or surgeon booking card (photo capture, `samplePaperCards.ts`) and survives in visual-card component and token names (`AsaCard`, `ControlCard`, `radius.card`, `motion.cardAdvance` …). RFP section titles quoted in the demo guide (`Card Copy`, `Card Immutability…`) stay verbatim as citations. "Permanent List" stays for Phase 30.
- **2026-10-02 · Copy is a skeleton-only new Booking** (**SUPERSEDED 2026-10-09 by catch-up Phase 15b: Copy a Booking is removed**, see below) (catch-up Phase 15; SUPERSEDES the 2026-07-22 Third external plan review #2 "Card Copy is the RFP's additional-procedure mechanism" and the `copyCard` part of the 2026-07-23 Phase 03 store additions). `copyBooking` makes a new Booking on the same List for the same patient with `copiedFromBookingId`, `source: 'copy'` and one fresh PRIMARY Procedure (`isAdditional: false`); it inherits nothing else. "References" in US-02.4.3 is read as the primary Procedure's `billingReference`, NOT `correlationRef` (a copy is a different appointment; sharing the correlation would let one hospital message hit two Bookings). This is the reading used, since the story does not define the word. The copy's `billingRoute` is the add-flow default `'hospital'`, never the source's, so the anaesthetist can complete it without the office (interim until Phase 20 replaces routes with the default hospital Contract). "Add another procedure" is the only additional-procedure path; the three wrappers open the new Booking.
- **2026-10-02 · `Booking.source` is optional and display-only** (catch-up Phase 15; DM-39; **AMENDED 2026-10-09 by Phase 15b:** the live values are `hospitalDownload`, `surgeonPdf`, `admin` and `anaesthetistAdHoc`; `'copy'` and `'anaesthetistPhoto'` are removed, and the Future-scope photo demo stamps `anaesthetistAdHoc`). No story requires a stored source and the audit trail records where each change came from, so no validator, guard, selector, billing module or review flag reads it, and later phases must not start to. Absent renders nothing. Interims: the HL7/FHIR S12 create stamps `hospitalDownload` until Phase 33 routes hospital rows through the matching screen; the post-op addendum's source follows the actor (`admin` for the office, else `anaesthetistAdHoc`) until Phase 39 replaces the addendum.
- **2026-10-09 · Copy a Booking is removed** (catch-up Phase 15b; SUPERSEDES 2026-10-02 "Copy is a skeleton-only new Booking"). US-02.4.3 was Retired on 2026-10-02 "and to be removed from the prototype"; Greg: redundant, a workaround for not being able to add a procedure to a Booking. `copyBooking`, `booking.copy`, `Booking.copiedFromBookingId`, the `'copy'` source, the "Copy booking" action and the copied-from banner are gone from all three apps. **Add another procedure** is the only way to add a Procedure for the same patient. The two July rulings that entry already superseded (2026-07-22 Third external plan review #2, the `copyCard` part of 2026-07-23 Phase 03 store additions) stay superseded.
- **2026-10-09 · Photo capture is Future Work; Add a booking opens on the manual form** (catch-up Phase 15b; US-02.4.4, RV-25; amends the photo half of 2026-07-23 "Phase 03 store additions"). The "Photo of paper list" choice left the Add a booking sheet on mobile, web and the office's phone-advice flow; with one way in, the sheet opens straight on the manual form titled "Add a booking" (`type.title`, one step above the form's section headings), with no chooser and no back chevron. `PhotoCaptureFlow` is kept only behind the badged "Photo capture (Future scope)" demo action on the mobile List (`photo-capture-future`, bar and PWA), through a UI-only request in `shared/demoTriggers/memory.ts`; the sheet then carries `DemoBadge tone="future"`.
- **2026-10-09 · The assigned List state is ACTIVE, not DRAFT** (catch-up Phase 15b; RV-36, EP-07, FT-07.1; SUPERSEDES binding convention 6's "DRAFT" for an assigned List). Renamed with no behaviour change: the same Lists are editable, submittable and authorisable by the same people. `ListState` is `'ACTIVE' | 'SUBMITTED' | 'AUTHORISED'`; `'DRAFT'` left the union until Phase 31 adds it back for Draft Lists. Refusal code `listNotActive` ("Only an active List can be submitted."). Labels come from `LIST_STATE_LABELS` (`shared/format.ts`); the Admin List drawer and the Move booking picker print no state on an empty free session (`isEmptyFreeSession`, `store/selectors.ts`).
- **2026-10-02 · Attachment ids are store-allocated** (catch-up Phase 15; SUPERSEDES the component-side index fix in the 2026-07-27 "Paired capture cards match heights; attachments can be removed" entry). Every attachment write goes through `addAttachment` / `removeAttachment` (`store/attachmentActions.ts`), ids are `AT####` from `allocateId`, display names no longer derive from ids, `editBooking` can no longer write attachments, and audit entries carry `{ attachmentId, name, kind }` only, never the data URL. A Free List holding attachments counts as booking context: it is not a `reassignList` target and `setAvailability` flags a conflict instead of restatusing it, so attachments are never absorbed silently.
- **2026-10-02 · Demo triggers live on their screen; the Control Panel is the index** (catch-up Phase 14; amends the Phase 12 control-panel layout). Every simulated event is a `DemoTrigger` in `src/shared/demoTriggers/registry.ts`, shown only on its route in the harness bar's single "Demo actions" pill (absent on screens with none) and, for PWA-surface entries, in the handset's Demo sheet. The Control Panel keeps Clock & reset and the S1 to S5 jumps (the 2026-07-28 clock entry stands) and lists every entry under its screen with an "Open screen" link; it carries no trigger buttons, and later phases never add one there. Its duplicate "Run payables" is dropped, because the Billing monitor's product button calls the same `runPayables(OFFICE)` and product actions stay in product UI.
- **2026-10-02 · "Play the office" defaults OFF, badged when on; "Office authorises this List" is the handset stand-in** (RV-22). Only a stored `'on'` reads ON (absent, corrupt or unreadable storage reads OFF); the More card says it is a scaffold and shows a "Simulated office" badge while on, and the Demo chip carries an "Office auto" marker. The per-List PWA-only entry calls the shared `authoriseAsSimulatedOffice` (`src/store/officeStandIn.ts`), which the timer also uses. Office stand-ins declare the PWA surface only; the framed build never auto-authorises.
- **2026-10-02 · HL7/FHIR tooling carries interim Future-scope badges until Phase 34** (RV-05, RV-06). The Integrations simulator header, the Admin Integrations Messages and Feed config tabs (tab label and panel note) and the two hospital-message demo actions are badged; Surgeon PDFs, Data quality and Validators stay unbadged (in scope). S1 carries the caveat in the Control Panel and the demo guide.
- **2026-10-02 · FT-13.5 is demonstrated as simulated audit rows; no sign-in splash.** "Simulate sign-in attempts" on Admin Audit appends five audit-only `mutate()` rows (entity `account`): provisioned with no credential access, Admin sign-in with MFA passed, a failed attempt, a self-service password reset (source anaesthetist: Dr Souter resets her own), and an Apple social-login sign-in on mobile. The IDaaS is not built; a splash, MFA screen or social buttons are out of scope unless the owner asks.
- **2026-09-28 · Anaesthetist Card shows no calculation; the Off / Units / Fee control is removed** (**SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-11-11 by catch-up Phase 20a (4):** the Contract's pricing basis now shows; the fee stays hidden) (user decision; supersedes the 2026-07-29 Off / Units / Fee entry below). The anaesthetist Card is fixed at the former **Off** behaviour on Mobile and Anaesthetist Web: no Card total, only Mark complete pinned, and the completion overlay shows the tick and "Card complete" alone. Office Admin Cards keep the full fee panel. Removed: the harness-bar `CardCalculationControl`, the PWA More panel's Card calculation card, `shell.cardCalculationMode` / `setCardCalculationMode`, the phone `CardTotalStrip` dock (dead once only anaesthetists use mobile; the mobile surface's `CardTotal` now renders nothing), and the Units display path in `CardTotalPanel`. No `PERSIST_VERSION` bump: a stale `cardCalculationMode` key in a persisted shell slice is carried by `backfillMerge` but never read. Demo guide S1 Beat 3, workflows, cheat sheet, README and master HTML updated.
- **2026-07-29 · Anaesthetist Card calculation has a persistent Off / Units / Fee presentation control** (user decision; superseded 2026-09-28). The global harness now shows all three directly selectable modes immediately before the app switcher. Fee is the default and preserves the signed-off full Card total; Units keeps the ticking unit count in a compact ink strip while removing rates, dollar totals, fee breakdowns, override-price notes and procedure-value chips; Off removes the calculation object and leaves only the completion action pinned. Mobile measures the resulting dock height, while the Anaesthetist Web rail keeps the units panel or button-only state sticky and aligned with the first capture cards. The completion animation follows the same privacy level. The choice persists across routes, app switches, reloads and Demo reset. Office Admin Cards deliberately keep the full fee presentation even when the global anaesthetist choice is Off or Units. This is a shell/presentation preference only: billing maths, domain data, lifecycle, audit, seed and `PERSIST_VERSION` are unchanged; current-version stores missing the new shell field backfill to Fee.
- **2026-07-29 · Every seeded Card carries a rich deterministic History trail** (user request; supersedes the 2026-07-23 minimal-seed decision below). A pristine reset now composes audit history over the FINAL schedule graph, including the Phase-10 historical billing Cards: each Card has a booking/create row, scheduling context where present, Procedure create and billing-setup rows, captured clinical values where present, BillingLine adds where present, and its completion or cancellation lifecycle fact. Existing pinned lifecycle audit remains authoritative and is deduplicated; generic and historical completed Cards gain their previously absent completion entry. Booking times are deterministically placed 6 to 14 days before the List with stable per-Card minutes and capped before the pinned reset clock, ordinary booking/setup provenance is Kirsty W. / office, integration-origin Cards retain system / integration provenance, and capture/completion provenance names the List anaesthetist. The combined seed log is chronologically sorted and reallocated as one sequential `A####` space so runtime mutation ids continue without collision. The result is **906** pristine entries across **170 Cards / 173 Procedures**; every Card History merges **4 to 9 rows**, instead of most Cards being empty. S5 still adds its three live Chen edits on top, but any Card can now demo History cold. The global viewer's existing 500-row cap and filters handle the larger feed. `PERSIST_VERSION` advances 9 → 10 so returning browsers receive the new audit graph and counter. The Data inspector empty state and S5 Markdown/HTML guide are updated. Regression coverage walks every Card, Procedure and fee line, proves completion/cancellation uniqueness, covers the historical `HC01`, chronological ids, pre-reset booking times and next-counter continuity, and keeps S5's live deltas pinned. Verified with `npm run build`, `npm run test` (**549** Vitest tests across 45 files), `npm run lint`, and the focused admin Phase-07 Playwright review/History flow; the rendered multi-day booking-to-completion ledger was visually checked.
- **2026-07-21 · Design run adopted as visual starting point** (user decision). Outputs in `docs/design/`; convention 17 added. Entries below capture its rulings.
- **2026-07-29 · Anaesthetist web Card total and completion action are separate controls with a curved sticky halo** (user decision and visual sign-off). The desktop commit rail now mirrors the mobile dock's visual hierarchy: the black Card total panel and teal **Mark complete** / completed-amend bar are separate siblings with an 8px gap and exactly matching widths. The sticky canvas backdrop extends 12px around the left, right and bottom without narrowing either control; its square top keeps scrolling content fully masked, while 26px lower corners continue the button's 14px curve through the 12px halo. The pair remains sticky and the total retains its alignment with the ASA status and Procedure code cards. The user confirmed the resulting concentric corner was "spot on". Mobile remains unchanged. Presentation only: no domain, store, seed, routing, lifecycle, billing, demo-script or `PERSIST_VERSION` change.
- **2026-07-29 · Refused Card completion moves to the first incomplete control** (user decision). On the mobile Card, selecting **Mark complete** with missing required billing data now keeps the existing summary and inline validation, then scrolls the Card's own content region to the first structured validator failure and moves keyboard focus to its actionable control. Billing context failures focus the Procedure Edit action; RVG/range, times, price-override and billing-line failures focus their corresponding capture control or card. Targets are scoped to the active Card so the mounted mobile slide stack cannot receive focus on a hidden sibling. Motion follows `prefers-reduced-motion`, and the focused target carries the semantic error outline. The shared Card body gives web the same validation affordance without changing validation order, domain/store behavior, seed content or `PERSIST_VERSION`. Demo-guide workflow and S1 presenter notes mirrored. Verified with `npm run build`, `npm run test` (**547** Vitest tests across 45 files), `npm run lint`, and a focused Playwright assertion that the incomplete Ellison Card scrolls to, focuses and reveals **Finish now** with its inline handover message.
- **2026-07-29 · Today outline belongs to the two schedule blocks, not the date label** (user decision). On the Anaesthetist web dashboard's week strip, the crimson today marker now wraps only the AM/PM List block pair; the day/date label remains above it in crimson text. The marker has equal 5px padding on all four sides, and the seven columns retain identical block insets and heights through transparent borders on non-today days. Presentation only: no store, seed, routing, lifecycle, billing or `PERSIST_VERSION` change.
- **2026-07-28 · Xero invoice pairs are routed, read-only drill-downs** (user decision). S3 Beat 2 no longer relies on a presenter pointing at an inert table row: `/demo/xero/invoices` lists each ACCREC/ACCPAY pair and `/demo/xero/invoices/:accRecId` shows the simulated collection invoice, payable bill, Xero InvoiceID/BillID and contact identifiers, line/totals and two-state money figures. Patient identity appears only in an explicitly separated "Linked Billing Engine case, not stored on the Xero contact" panel; no NHI enters the derived view. Invoice numbers and `View pair` are real links, Back/refresh work, stale ids fall back to the collection, and incomplete pair/contact data renders a diagnostic instead of blanking. Contacts remain a read-only reference and payment/payables mutations remain in the established control-panel/Admin flows. No domain/store schema or `PERSIST_VERSION` change. The S3 script and master guide now name the exact click path. Verified with `npm run build`, `npm run test` (**547** Vitest tests across 45 files), `npm run lint`, and the new focused Playwright S3 drill-down (including refresh, Back, stale-id recovery and no displayed NHI).
- **2026-07-28 · Invoice preview centred with a sticky information rail** (user decision). The 760px printable invoice now sits in a centred 1,048px desktop workspace with a 24px gap and a 264px rail. The rail stays 24px from the top, holds local 40px Email/Print controls, keeps insurer presentation as status rather than an invented portal action, and separates the Xero ACCREC and ACCPAY references into labelled rows. Emailed, pending and failed-handoff states remain visible there; failure stays amber and points to Billing monitor. Breadcrumbs align to the same workspace, while browser printing still isolates only the invoice document. No domain/store schema, shared button default or `PERSIST_VERSION` change.
- **2026-07-28 · Build-phase scaffolding removed from rendered app copy** (user decision). Completed capabilities no longer describe themselves by prototype phase, and non-functional placeholder controls are not shown as real actions. Honest simulation boundaries such as "referenced, not implemented" remain where they explain deliberately excluded external integrations. Historical seed-copy changed, so `PERSIST_VERSION` advances 8 → 9.

The blank NHI lookup is enabled only for Dr Priya Sharma's Tue 21 PM phone-advice path after St George's and Mr T. Hale are selected. One click returns a unique valid fictional NHI and fills the patient, phone, operation/code, scheduled time, Hospital route, informational insurer and billing reference, with every value still editable. - **2026-07-28 · Demo clock promoted into the global harness** (user decision). The presenter no longer leaves the screen being demonstrated just to advance time: a compact clock icon + live `h:mm` control now sits immediately to the right of the app switcher on every app and demo surface. Its popover carries all six established shortcuts (`+15 min`, `+1 hour`, `Next day`, `Next morning`, `+7 days`, `Procedure day · 28 Jul`), remains open for consecutive jumps, updates live through the existing persisted Zustand clock, and never navigates or reloads the current screen. The original control-panel clock and reset remain as the explanatory/recovery surface. - **2026-07-24 · Phase 13 final visual pick: "Brand whisper"; lab hidden behind a button; avatar contrast fixed** (user decisions). The user chose the faintest brand-crimson preset ("Brand whisper": `#ECCED5` at opacity 0.45, broad, fading by 84%) as the shipped default. The Gradient Lab now starts collapsed behind its toggle button on every viewport (it is a temporary tuning tool, kept out of the presentation). Because the crimson-tint avatar blended into the new crimson wash, the persona avatar was reworked (via a new shared `Avatar` component) to an **elevated-white chip** — the user's pick from a standalone 10-option comparison page (`aa-prototype/avatar-options.html`, non-routed): white fill, crimson initials, no ring, carrying the list cards' `elevation.e1` shadow so it lifts off the wash and white cards alike by elevation rather than colour. Applied to the header, the More profile card and the "My availability" avatars; colleague-list avatars keep the tint chip (a "you vs others" distinction). The default is now a SINGLE `accent.tint` teal wash from the top ("Teal dawn") — teal is the app's own accent, so a lone teal reads clinical and unmistakably AA, white-first. The lab gained a `GRADIENT_PRESETS` grid of ten deliberate ideas to switch between and review (six single-teal placements, two weak warm-blush singles, a near-colourless neutral "mist", and a flat baseline); the two field controls were relabelled Primary/Secondary (any hue can go in either). - **2026-07-24 · Phase 10 build — decisions.** (1) **Money source of truth = three cumulative amounts on `BillingCase`** (`receivedAmount`/`authorisedAmount`/`disbursedAmount` + `paidInAtISO`/`disbursedAtISO`); `status` is a derived label (paid-in and disbursed are two independent axes). Pro-rata authorisation is **cumulative-rounded** (`proRataAuthorised = round2(min(received/amountDue,1) × accPayTotal)`, `accPayTotal == amountDue`), so authorised == received with no drift; payables pay `authorised − disbursed` (no double-pay; `payablesActions.test.ts`). (2) **Handoff (`store/xeroHandoff.ts`)** is idempotent (accRecId set → no-op), **folded into `wireBillingRun`** (runs after the run's synchronous commit, reads committed cases via fresh `getState()`) and called from `raisePreProcedureInvoice` (pre-invoice → **full ACCREC+ACCPAY pair**, D-pre-invoice-pair, so a fully-prepaid procedure still has a disbursement path). A **handoff fault is data, not a throw** (`case.handoffFailure` + clear `failNextHandoff` + no pair + `status:'invoiced'`, one mutate); its retry re-invokes the idempotent handoff — distinct from `retryBillingCase` (rebuilds invoices, keys off `status:'failed'`). A **billing-failure resolve-&-retry then hands off** (monitor), else the rebuilt invoice would never become payable (review-fix + test). (3) **Contact resolution (Appendix 2):** cached `ContactID` (`billing.contactIdCache`) → lookup by `ContactNumber` → create; orgs (hospital/insurer/surgeon/organisation → `organisation` type) keyed by holder id, never archived; patients on `hiddenInternalId`; billableParties on their own hidden id; an **archived match is unarchived** with the "unarchive TBC in sandbox" note (the plan's Step-1 ruling; the RFP-literal "invoice directly against the archived contact" is the alternative TBC branch). (4) **Payment detection (`paymentActions.ts` + `reconciliationPoll.ts`):** webhook + daily poll write through ONE handler, **idempotent by the receipts-ledger key**; a poll-reconciled receipt is dated the payment's OWN date (not the detection day) so it lands in the correct GST period (review-fix + test). Overpayment is clamped to the balance due (protects conservation; unreachable via the derived-amount demo control). - **2026-07-24 · Persisted-store rehydration hardened (bug fix, `store/appStore.ts`).** A running-app crash (`DemoXero` blank screen, `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'softLimit')`) traced to how the persisted store rehydrates, NOT to stale seed data. Two mechanisms, now both guarded: (1) a **different-version** store is reseeded by `migrate` (returns `freshAppState()`) — as intended by the PERSIST_VERSION convention; (2) a store at the **current** version but an **older shape** (a nested field added within a version, or a shape change that forgot to bump — e.g. a v6 store persisted mid-Phase-10 before `settings.volumeStory` existed) takes the no-migrate path, where zustand's **default merge is a shallow spread** that let the incomplete persisted `settings` clobber the fresh one, dropping `volumeStory` → crash. Fix: a `merge` (`backfillMerge`) that overlays persisted onto fresh **one level deep**, so every slice's sub-keys always exist (persisted/live values win where present, seed fills the gaps). Deliberately exactly one level: record maps live one level down and are copied wholesale, so a demo-deleted record is never resurrected; deep record-SHAPE changes still require a version bump. Regression tests in `persistMigrate.test.ts` cover version-mismatch reseed, same-version backfill, current-version round-trip, and no-resurrection. **The earlier "add a migrate" fix was necessary but not sufficient** — it only covered path (1); the user's store was on path (2), which is why clearing the HTTP cache + hard-reloading (neither of which clears localStorage) still crashed. With this fix a plain reload suffices; no localStorage clear or Reset needed. `tsc -b` + `npm run build` + `npx oxlint` clean, **419** vitest tests.

- **SUPERSEDED 2026-11-11 by catch-up Phase 19b (OQ-95 part 2): no stacking limit and no band rule; the age band is pre-applied, its boundaries D29's default.** **2026-07-27 · Modifier bands — one code per band (a picked reading; the RFP does not state it).** A demo card was found carrying **both A1 "very old" and A2 "very young"**, summing to M = 3 for one patient; the same stacking was reachable across the BMI ladder, the pre-assessment ladder and the ASA codes, because `ModifierChips.toggle` appended freely and `modifierUnits` summed whatever it was handed. **The RFP never states mutual exclusivity, but its own arithmetic requires it:** the modifier table (`RFP.md:1061-1105`) is organised by "Modifier group" with an **"Example range" per group** (PA 1 to 4, A 1 to 2, AS 0 to 4, OB 0 to 3), and those ranges are each group's min-to-max contribution, only reachable if exactly one code per group applies — stacking takes OB to 6, A to 3 and PA to 11. Supporting wording: modifiers "depend on a score or category" (`:1051`), which is single-valued, and "body mass index **banding**"; the RFP already single-selects ASA by giving it its own field that seeds M (`:1054-1059`). **The rule:** `PA1-PA4`, `A`, `AS` and `OB` are exclusive bands (`EXCLUSIVE_MODIFIER_GROUPS` in `modifierCodes.ts`, one line of RFP basis per row); `ASE`, `P1`, `AI1` and the POSTOP pair stack, post-op being "separately itemised, sometimes days later" (`:1103`). **PA5 is the one exemption inside a banded group** (`STACKS_WITHIN_GROUP`): it is a distinct LATER contact, as our own label ("Phone follow-up") says, not an alternative assessment type. That is a **deliberate, recorded deviation** — PA can then reach 5 units (PA4 + PA5), one above the RFP's stated 1 to 4 range — and because the range arithmetic is the whole argument for the rule, the docs state the exception rather than glossing it; it forms part of the question to AA. **Two layers, mirroring the existing P1-absorption pattern:** the picker is primary and **swaps on tap** (turning a chip on drops its selected sibling first, so one tap moves OB2 → OB3; siblings are deliberately NOT disabled, which would make changing a band a two-tap dead end), and the domain is the backstop — `modifierUnits` keeps the **first** code of a band and refuses the rest with a verbatim reason ("A2 is not added: A1 already covers the age-extreme band · only one applies per procedure."), so data that bypassed the picker (persisted pre-fix state, a future integration, the seed) can never double-count. First-wins is deterministic and preserves the precedence `fee.ts` already had (it appends `procedure.asaClass` only when the selection does not carry it), which closes a real if currently unreachable double-count: an `asaClass` plus a stale selected AS code now resolves to one ASA value instead of two. The band is claimed by the first code SEEN, absorbed or not, so an absorbed code cannot hand its band to a sibling. **No new `validateCardForBilling` rule:** with swap-on-tap a collision is not user-reachable and the domain refusal already prevents mis-pricing, so a completion blocker would invent a failure mode users cannot hit. The pure selection rule lives in the domain as `toggleModifierCode` (unit-testable; the chip component stays a renderer). **Review finding 06.5 folded in** (CONFIRMED, cosmetic — the M-row caption credited units the base code absorbs while the M total correctly excluded them): `modifierBreakdown` now takes `btm.refusedModifiers` and skips every refused code, so the caption and the M total can no longer disagree. Surfaced on screen as a **Selection** column ("Pick one" / "Adds on top") on the admin Modifier codes master tab, with the header copy saying the rule is a reading of the RFP's group ranges rather than stated text — the same way every other §11 discovery item is presented. **`PERSIST_VERSION` 7 → 8**: the seed's own content is unchanged (it sets a single code, `cards.ts:408`), but a collision already clicked into a demo machine's persisted state would otherwise survive the reload and render a refusal caption mid-demo. Recorded in `prototype-review/12-RFP-CONFLICTS-AND-CHOICES.md` (section 3 + new question 21) rather than review 11, whose 44-claim tally and verdict counts are dated provenance; `REQUIREMENTS.md` B3, cheat-sheet item 10, the workflow's capture steps and `master-demo-guide.html` all carry the sibling rule.
