- **2026-07-27 · Audit history presentation — the change ledger, newest-first, and view-only coalescing (review findings 01.3 and 02.3).** The Card History sheet and the admin Audit viewer both rendered `JSON.stringify` of the patch: a run of four stepper taps on the B row read as four rows of `{"baseUnitsCaptured":{"units":4,"source":"overridden"}} to {…}`, all stamped `2026-07-21 08:00:00`. The data underneath was correct and complete; the presentation was unreadable, on the surface AA is shown as the answer to **A7**. **One genuine defect, five presentation faults.** The defect: `editCard` / `editProcedure` build `before` as `Object.fromEntries(Object.keys(patch).map(k => [k, entity[k]]))`, so a field that was never set arrives as a PRESENT key holding `undefined` — and `JSON.stringify` drops it, which is why "not previously set" and "cleared" both printed as `{}`. The fix diffs over the **union of both sides' keys**, so the key survives and renders as `not set`. **New shared module `src/shared/audit/`** (pure, 24 Vitest cases — `formatAuditChange` never had one): `actionLabels.ts` (every action code the store or seed can emit, with a source-scanning test that fails if one is added unlabelled, plus an `entity.verb` → "Entity verb" fallback), `fieldLabels.ts` (patch keys of Card / Procedure / List / Contract / ContractPrice / Patient / Anaesthetist / BillingLine plus the audit-only synthetic keys, camelCase fallback), `auditNarrative.ts` (`auditFieldChanges`, `formatAuditValue` for the nested shapes — `CapturedUnits`, `PriceOverride`, `PrepaymentDetail`, `CounterpartyRef`, `ContractScope`, string arrays, ISO stamps, money — `sortAuditNewestFirst`, `coalesceAudit`, `summariseAuditChanges`). **No JSON path remains**: an unrecognised object degrades to its labelled leading fields, so a shape added later reads as English rather than braces. **Three rulings, recorded so they are not re-litigated.** (1) **Coalescing is a VIEW, never a write** — consecutive entries sharing actor, action, entity, timestamp and a single changed key collapse into one row stating the net movement (first `before` → last `after`) with a count chip and a "Show the 4 steps" toggle; the append-only trail is untouched, so A7 still holds, and expanding shows every stored tap. The write-through-per-tap capture strategy (`BtmCaptureBlock`, a logged decision) is deliberately NOT changed — it is what makes the trail reconstructable; this was a presentation fix only. (2) **Newest first on both surfaces, sorted on `atISO` with the sequential audit id as the tiebreak** (closes 01.3, which found the viewer using insertion order and the two surfaces disagreeing on direction). The tiebreak is load-bearing, not cosmetic: the demo clock is pinned, so every entry a presenter creates live shares one timestamp and the id is the only thing preserving the order the taps happened in. The top row now IS the record's last change, which incidentally renders what 02.3 flags as stamped-but-never-shown (`lastModifiedBy` / `lastModifiedAt`); no pinned header was added. **Known interaction with the pinned clock:** live edits stamp 08:00, so on a Card carrying a seeded afternoon completion (S5's Chen Card, 16:02) the staged edits sort BELOW it — chronological is right and insertion order was the bug, so the sort stands; a presenter wanting the edits on top can advance the demo clock before staging. (3) **The Audit viewer keeps a compact one-line change cell** ("Base units 4 → 1", extra fields as `+2 more`) with the human label leading the Action cell and the machine code beneath it — the compliance surface stays greppable and a 500-row feed stays scannable, while the full field ledger lives on the Card sheet where someone is reading one record. It also never collapses `Role · source` and never coalesces; the Card sheet prints `Dr Melanie Souter · anaesthetist` when role and source agree and `webPAS · system · integration` when they differ. **The design work is structural, not chromatic** (convention 17): no new palette, no new type, no semantic colour — nothing in a history is a warning, and tinting rows would imply a judgement the audit does not make. `HistoryTimeline` was rewritten to render a micro-caps day heading (reusing `dayHeading`), a **suppressed time gutter** (the `HH:MM` blanks when identical to the row above, so twelve 08:00 taps read as one moment instead of a broken clock, and ~76px of width comes back on the phone), and the **change ledger** — one line per field, `LABEL  old → new`, values in tabular mono aligned on a 108px label column so a numeric ratchet forms a visible staircase. Below 300px of measured content width (a `ResizeObserver`, because inline styles carry no media queries) the ledger stacks the label above the values rather than breaking the alignment; the threshold is what the aligned form costs, so the 390px design phone keeps it and only a genuinely cramped window stacks. `→` is house-legal user-facing copy already shipping in `TimesCard` — the CLAUDE.md ban covers en and em dashes only. One motion: the group expand transitions `grid-template-rows` on `motion.sheetIn`; reduced motion collapses it to the global 80ms fade. Optional `entityLabels` thread from `CardDetailBody` and `ReviewScreen` so a **multi**-procedure Card's rows say "Procedure 1 · Left total hip replacement"; a single-procedure Card gets no scope line, and `ListDrawer` (one List entity) passes none. `formatAuditChange` and its private `auditValue` are deleted from `format.ts`. No seed shape or content change, so **no `PERSIST_VERSION` bump**. Still open, deliberately out of scope and worth its own piece of work: on a pristine reset the seeded trail is thin (finding 04.3 — 37 audit rows against ~170 Cards), so the sheet is now legible but still short until the S5 jump or a few live edits populate it. `tsc -b` + `npm run build` + `npx oxlint` clean, **543** vitest tests across 44 files (the 24 new `auditNarrative.test.ts` cases plus a concurrent session's), **39** Playwright specs green including regenerated `a7-08-history.png` / `a7-07-audit.png`; browser-verified on the real app for the four-tap ratchet (net `not set → 3`, four steps behind the toggle), the "back to the seeded value" reset, a multi-procedure Card's scope lines, the S5 Chen trail, the 340px stacked fallback and reduced motion.

- **2026-07-27 · The scheduled slot is a row in the Patient card, not a card of its own** (user finding on the new desktop layout: "why do we have two timer boxes, one in the main column and one in the rail?"). `card.scheduledTime` had a `Section` to itself carrying a 24px mono value and two 44px steppers, which put it at the same visual weight as `TimesCard` — and once the desktop set the rail beside the capture column, the two read as two versions of one control. They are not: the slot is the plan (Card-level, one value however many procedures, from the theatre list, no effect on money), while Start/Handover are what happened (per procedure, stamped from the demo clock, the source of the time units and therefore the fee). Nothing reconciles them and nothing should — "Start now" deliberately works before the scheduled time, because the clock is the authority for what happened and the slot is only where the patient was penciled in. **Demoted rather than relabelled** (the alternative considered was sharper labels, "Scheduled slot" vs "Anaesthetic times", which explains a hierarchy problem instead of fixing it): the slot is now a `Scheduled` row inside the Patient section, aligned on the same 96px label column as NHI / Date of birth / Contact and set in the same 14px mono, so it reads as reference data beside the identity it belongs to. **The ±5 steppers stay on the row at 44px** rather than moving behind an Edit sheet — a slipping list is nudged in passing, and a three-tap correction on the phone would be a worse trade than the row height; they gained the `aria-label`s they never had ("5 minutes earlier" / "5 minutes later"), since the value they act on is no longer the only thing in the box. **Applied to BOTH surfaces, not gated on `feePlacement`-style capability:** no mockup covers a scheduled-time card, so nothing in `docs/design/` is being contradicted, the rhyme exists on the phone too (only separated by scroll rather than side by side), and the phone gets ~100px of scroll back. No demo-guide beat touches these steppers (S1's "scheduled time 15:00" is the manual card form). No store, seed or `PERSIST_VERSION` change — presentation only. `tsc -b` + `npm run build` + `npx oxlint` clean, **543** vitest tests across 44 files, **49** Playwright specs; browser-verified on web and mobile, including that the nudge still writes through `editCard` (16:00 → 16:05 → 15:55).

- **2026-07-27 · Real routing inside the three apps — deliberately REVERSING both 2026-07-23 navigation rulings** ("Mobile navigation is a local translateX stack, not router routes" and "Web navigation is app-owned local state, not router sub-routes"; user decision). **The problem:** refreshing lost your place. `router.tsx` was already a real `BrowserRouter` and `AppShell` already treated the URL as the source of truth for which app was showing, so a refresh kept the right *app* — but every per-app screen lived in `useState` (web: `tab`, `drill.listId`, `drill.cardId`, `accountsSubTab`, `weekOffset`; admin: `section`, `selectedDate`, `sortMode`, `cardDetailId`, `reviewListId`, `invoiceId`; mobile: `tab`, `listId`, `cardId`, `depth`), so a reload dumped you back on the Dashboard, the Day view or the Lists tab. **The shape:** each app is now a LAYOUT route with its screens nested beneath it, and `router.tsx` carries the whole URL map in one readable place (`/web/lists/:listId/cards/:cardId`, `/web/accounts/:subTab`, `/admin/day/:dateISO/cards/:cardId`, `/admin/review/:listId`, `/admin/invoices/:invoiceId`, `/mobile/lists/*` …). The layouts pass their derivations down through `<Outlet context>` (typed in a per-app `outlet.ts`, kept out of the component files so fast refresh still works), and one thin wrapper per screen in a per-app `routes.tsx` turns URL params into props and the screens' existing `onBack`/`onOpenList`/`onOpenCard` callbacks into `navigate()` calls. **No screen changed** — only the three app roots, three new `routes.tsx`, three new `outlet.ts` and `router.tsx`. **The split we picked:** path segments carry NAVIGATION; query params carry VIEW PREFERENCES. Two things are preferences, not steps — the admin day grid's row order (`?sort=az`) and the web dashboard's week strip, which became an explicit Monday anchor (`?week=2026-07-27`) rather than an offset so a shared URL does not depend on where the demo clock is. Both are written with `replace`, so Back is never a preference toggle; the admin `:dateISO` is a path segment, so day stepping IS undoable with Back. **Transient overlays stay local `useState`** — `RequestCoverSheet`, `AddCardFlow`, the mobile offer sheet and the admin `ListDrawer`: a sheet in the URL makes Back close the sheet instead of going back a screen, which reads as broken. **Mobile keeps its choreography, and the 2026-07-23 ruling's technical reason is UPHELD:** sibling routes per layer would unmount the outgoing screen and kill the pop, because `SlideStack` keeps all three layers mounted and animates by `transform` at `motion.cardAdvance` (260ms in / 240ms return). So the Lists tab is ONE splat route hosting the stack, with depth and ids derived from the URL (`matchPath` in the new `apps/mobile/navigation.ts`, shared with the shell so the tab bar hides at depth > 0) and the last-seen ids held in a ref that is NEVER cleared — an exact port of the old `onBack={() => setDepth(0)}`, which likewise moved depth and left `listId`/`cardId` in place so the layer could slide out. **Index routes preserved** (the load-bearing constraint): `/mobile`, `/web` and `/admin` all stay valid, redirecting to `lists`, rendering the dashboard, and redirecting to `day/<today>` — so `APP_CONFIG[...].path`, `RootRedirect`, the app switcher and all 39 pre-existing Playwright specs are untouched. `appIdForPath()` already matched `pathname.startsWith(path + '/')`, so `AppShell` needed no change at all. **Stale ids** (a URL outlives the seed it was copied from): the shared `RequireEntity` (`src/shell/RequireEntity.tsx`) redirects a `:listId`/`:cardId`/`:invoiceId` the current data no longer holds to its parent route, replacing the blank screen the screens' `return null` guards produced — `:listId`/`:cardId`/`:invoiceId` routes are nested one segment deep under the collection they fall back to, because React Router's relative `..` is route-relative, not path-relative. A junk `:dateISO` or `?week=` is rejected by the new `isISODate` (`src/shell/routeParams.ts`) and falls back to the demo clock, since `format(parseISO('nope'))` throws. **Two behaviour changes that came free:** the admin List drawer now closes on ANY route change (the old `RightRail.onReviewList` set the section without clearing `drawerListId`, leaving the drawer open over the review screen), and admin date navigation is undoable with Back. **Deliberately NOT promoted** (still local state, no demo beat links to them): mobile `BalancesScreen`'s `section` and admin `IntegrationMonitorScreen`'s `tab`. Also added `aa-prototype/vercel.json` (SPA rewrite) — Vite dev and preview already serve `index.html` for unknown paths, but on a static host a refreshed deep link would 404, which is the very bug being fixed. **No `PERSIST_VERSION` bump** (seed shape unchanged) and `shell.currentApp` untouched. `tsc -b` + `npm run build` + `npx oxlint` clean, **543** vitest tests across 44 files (logic-only, structurally unaffected), **52** Playwright specs — 13 new in `visual/routing.spec.ts` covering deep-link entry, `page.reload()` staying put, Back unwinding a drill, the `?sort` / `?week` round trip, the remembered admin day + order, the stale-id fallbacks, and that a mobile pop still ANIMATES (the outgoing layer stays mounted and its computed transform moves through several values on the way off-screen; `SlideStack` layers gained a `data-testid` to make that assertable). `docs/demo-guide/03-demo-script.md` and `master-demo-guide.html` gained a **Direct URLs** table per app — the practical payoff, since a presenter can now jump straight to a beat and a stray refresh no longer costs the thread.

- **2026-07-27 · Paired capture cards match heights; attachments can be removed** (three user findings on the desktop card detail). **(1) `Pair` now stretches by default.** It was `align-items: start` on the reasoning that a stretched shorter card ends in a pane of empty white; the user's screenshots say the ragged bottom edge is the worse of the two, and they are right — two white cards on one row that stop at different heights read as a rendering fault, whereas white space inside a card is just a card. The slack is absorbed rather than left stranded: **`CaptureSection` gains a `footer` slot** that renders on `margin-top: auto`, so a stretched card's caption or trailing action sinks to its foot instead of floating mid-card. Four cards declare one — ASA's seeding caption, the procedure code's P1 note and failures, the override's Save + caption + failures, and the billing lines' Add button + failures — which is why the ASA and procedure-code captions now sit on one line, and why "Add billing line" anchors to the foot of a card matched against a much taller Adjustment card. A caller passes **`null`, not a fragment of conditionals**, when its footer is empty, because an always-truthy wrapper still costs one `gap` of trailing space. **`align="start"` survives as the exception** and `TimesCard` is its only user: its two halves are content blocks inside one card, not two cards, so matching them would stretch a grey duration strip around its two lines with no border to justify the height. **Mobile is untouched by all of it** — nothing stretches in a single column, so the footer slot is inert and the cards render exactly as before (screenshot-verified). **(2) Attachments can be removed:** a 24px × on the thumbnail's corner (`canEdit` only), because the target should be the thing it deletes rather than a row of Remove links, and small and cornered because a scan is dropped rarely and by mistake never. It writes through `editCard`, so the removal is audited like any other Card edit and needs no new store action. **Hidden until the thumbnail is hovered** (user request), so a row of scans reads as scans rather than as a row of delete buttons; it **stays mounted at `opacity: 0`** rather than being conditionally rendered, and focus reveals it as hover does, which is what keeps it reachable by keyboard instead of being a mouse-only action. The 120ms fade collapses to the global 80ms under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Worth knowing before this pattern spreads: hover-reveal has no equivalent on a real touch device, so it works here because both apps are demoed in a desktop browser (the phone is a frame, not a phone) and because Remove is a correction, not a step in any workflow. **The add path had a latent id collision** that only removal could expose: `addPhoto` named the next photo from the attachment COUNT, so removing Photo 2 of 3 and adding again produced a second `C0009-A3` — one id on two attachments, and Remove would take both. It now counts one past the highest index the Card has ever used, which also keeps the row in ascending order (`Photo 1 · Photo 3 · Photo 4`), so a removal reads as a missing number rather than a shuffled one. No token, colour or copy-rule change; no seed or `PERSIST_VERSION` change. New Playwright spec `visual/card-attachments.spec.ts` pins both pairs' heights (bounding boxes within 1px) and the add / remove / re-add index cycle, since the id allocation lives in the component and no Vitest test reaches it. `tsc -b` + `npm run build` + `npm run lint` clean, **543** vitest tests across 44 files, **54** Playwright specs.

- **SUPERSEDED 2026-11-11 by catch-up Phase 19b: the itemised Modifiers ledger and the picker with an inline explanation replace the segmented bands and "Also applies" chips.** **2026-07-28 · Modifier picker: the shape of the control now states the rule** (user decision, after a brainstorm and two interactive option pages). **The problem:** `ModifierChips` rendered all 16 codes (the 20-code master minus the 4 ASA codes) as one identical flex-wrap chip row. On the phone that is ~15 rows, taller than the viewport and taller than the M row's own prose caption of the same selection; on the desktop's 832px capture column it is 5 to 6 ragged rows. Neither told the user which codes are alternatives and which add up, so the band swap (Decisions log 2026-07-27) read as a chip switching itself off. **The fix, picked from ten costed options: band controls (option 1) + short labels (option 5).** The three exclusive bands the picker owns (PA, A, OB — 'AS' belongs to `AsaCard`) are now SEGMENTED CONTROLS, the pattern `AsaCard` already uses for the fourth exclusive band; the six free-stacking codes (PA5, ASE, P1, AI1, PO1, PO2) keep chips, so a chip on this card now means exactly one thing: something that adds on top. Chip labels dropped the code prefix, which was redundant beside the band title and is still carried by the M row's caption and the audit trail. Ten of the sixteen chips are absorbed that way. **Two surfaces, two arrangements, one component** (keyed off `useSurface().variant`, as `Pair` and `feePlacement` already are), because the problem differs: mobile was fighting height (label above a two-column segment grid, unit stacked under the label, ~15 rows to 4), desktop was fighting structure (label column | control, so the four band labels align with each other and with the B / T / M rows above, plus a hairline marking the seam between the seeded arithmetic and the clinical facts that drive it). **Measured honestly: the desktop block is slightly TALLER than the chip wall** (314px against 266px at a 1440px window) and that is the accepted trade — height was never the desktop problem, the block sits in an 832px column beside the pinned rail. **No measurement code and no ResizeObserver:** a desktop band control is `inline-flex` + `wrap`, so it is as wide as its segments need and no wider (a two-option band is never stretched into two slabs) and a segment that cannot fit its row wraps inside its own track rather than shrinking below its own words. Verified at 1440 / 1180 / 1024 / 900 / 780 with zero clipped labels; the app's own layout floors the card at 779px, so the wrap path is a safety net rather than a state the demo will show. **The domain is unchanged and stays the authority:** `BANDS` and `STACKING_CODES` are derived from `modifierBandOf` rather than a list of the component's own, so the picker cannot disagree with the calculator about what is exclusive; `toggleModifierCode` still performs the swap, and re-tapping the live segment still clears the band exactly as re-tapping the old chip did. Absorbed codes stay visible but inert and struck through with the domain's verbatim refusal reason, now on segments as well as chips. `aria-pressed` added to both. New `MODIFIER_BAND_TITLES` + `MODIFIER_SEGMENT_LABELS` in `modifierLabels.ts` (the band title carries the subject, so the BMI segments read "Under 30 / 30 to 35 / 35 to 40 / Over 40"). No store, seed, lifecycle, billing or `PERSIST_VERSION` change. `npm run build` + `npx vitest run` clean, **543** Vitest tests across 44 files. Demo guide mirrored (`02-workflows-and-handoffs.md` step 8, `master-demo-guide.html` fee-calculation list). The two decision aids that produced the choice are kept at `aa-prototype/modifier-options.html` (phone, 10 options measured) and `aa-prototype/modifier-options-web.html` (desktop, 3 options at three window widths) — standalone files outside the router and the Vite build input, like `avatar-options.html`.

- **2026-07-28 · The phone pins the Card total too, and the masthead folds to pay for it — REVERSING `feePlacement: 'inline'`** (user decision, after a brainstorm and one interactive option page). **The problem:** the desktop pins the ink calculation block to the top of the commit rail, so a modifier tap ticks the fee in place; the phone put a `FeeSummaryPanel` inline under each capture block, which meant the tap that changed the number and the number itself were rarely on screen together. The value-tick — the design's own named motion pattern, and the beat the workshop is built on — played where nobody was looking. **What was in the way:** a pinned total costs ~72px, and the 2026-07-27 finding forbids showing the figure twice on a one-procedure Card, so the inline panel had to go with it; and a Card can carry several procedures, which is exactly why the panel was per-procedure in the first place. **The fix, picked from ten costed options: the two-tier dock (option 3) + procedure chips (option 8) + a folding masthead.** (1) New `CardTotalStrip` — `CardTotalPanel` reduced to the two figures that move (units left, rate + fee right), with `CompleteBar` below it, both inside the existing blurred `14 / 20 / 32` footer. (2) The procedures become a row of mono chips (`P1 $291.50`) inside the same ink object rather than a stacked row each, so **the dock is the same height for one procedure or five** — that fixed height is what makes pinning affordable at all on 844px. A one-procedure Card shows no chip row, so the common case pays nothing for the rare one; past three procedures the row states the count instead of clipping silently. (3) The masthead **folds**: at rest the name over a status chip and the operation, past 24px of scroll a 44px nav row carrying the name inline beside the back link, iOS large-title fashion. The **NHI and date of birth left the header entirely** — they were duplicated verbatim by the Patient card two rows down, which is the card's one home for patient reference data. **Measured live in the app, not asserted:** masthead 181px at rest and **119px folded**, dock **175px**, so **550px of working room against ~525px before** — the phone ends up with MORE room than it had when the total sat inline, and the money is now permanently on screen. Two procedures: dock 213px, room 511px. **Seam changes.** `feePlacement` is **deleted**, not flipped: with both surfaces pinning, the field had one value and no branch, so the honest statement is that money is always pinned. `FeeSummaryPanel.tsx` is deleted with it. `Surface` gains **`CardTotal`** (mobile `CardTotalStrip`, web `CardTotalPanel`) alongside `Overlay` / `CardLayout` / `Pair`, so `CardDetailBody` still names the pieces and never branches on platform; `CardTotalLine` + the new shared `CardTotalProps` move into `surface/context.ts`, which is where the seam's contracts live. `CardLayoutSlots` gains **`header: ((collapsed: boolean) => ReactNode) | null`** — the masthead is handed to the layout rather than rendered above it, because the scroll region it reacts to belongs to `MobileCardLayout`; web and admin keep their own page headers and pass null. `CardTotalProps.linesArePerProcedure` distinguishes per-procedure rows from one procedure's several fee lines, because the strip may chip the first and cannot chip the second (a fee line has no ordinal to name it by); the rail ignores it, since its labels carry the meaning either way. **Two mechanical details worth keeping:** the dock's bottom clearance is **measured** with a `ResizeObserver` (a constant was safe while the dock was only ever a 56px button, and would now either strand content behind it or leave a gap), and the fold uses **two thresholds** (collapse at 24, expand at 6) because collapsing lengthens the scroll region and one threshold can hand back a scrollTop that immediately unfolds it. The fold borrows `cardAdvance`'s curve and return duration, the closest of the four named patterns; `global.css` already flattens it under `prefers-reduced-motion`. **Not built, and deliberately:** the demo page's "lit chip for the procedure you are editing" needs per-block scroll tracking threaded through the shared body, which is fragility for a highlight. **No domain, store, seed, lifecycle, billing or `PERSIST_VERSION` change** — `cardFee` was already the pinned figure on the desktop. `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, **543** Vitest tests across 44 files and **54** Playwright specs all green; `mobile-phase04.spec.ts` swapped its `TOTAL UNITS` anchor (the deleted inline panel) for the folded-masthead shot. - **2026-08-03 · The installed PWA takes the full screen: `black-translucent` status bar, plus the measured viewport correction it forces** (user-reported, settled by measurement on an iPhone 16 Pro, iOS 18.7 / Safari 26.5.2, 402x874pt). **Symptom 1:** under the shipped `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style: default`, iOS kept the status bar OUTSIDE the web view, started the view below it, and painted the reserved band with the document background. Sampled off the handset screenshots, that band was a flat `#F5F8F7` (`neutral.bg`) down to y=138 while the atmosphere began beneath it: a hard seam across the top of every screen. A reserved band is also not a safe area, so `env(safe-area-inset-top)` reported **0** and `--aa-inset-top` sat on its 12px floor, costing the canvas a full status bar off the bottom as well. **Fix 1:** `black-translucent`, which starts the view at y=0 so the atmosphere flows under the status bar exactly as it does under the frame's fake one, and reports the device's real 62px for the inset contract to consume. Glyph colour was the one genuine risk and is now OBSERVED, not assumed: iOS renders dark glyphs over the light wash, and they stay legible with a sheet open (`scrim` is `rgba(23,35,32,0.32)`, which composites the wash to about `#ACABAA` and leaves dark glyphs near 9:1). **The deployment trap, which cost two rounds:** iOS builds the standalone window, geometry and status-bar style included, when the web view is created AT LAUNCH from the HTML it loads then. A service-worker update swaps the content of a running app, so the More tab's Build card correctly reported the new build while the window was still laid out to the old chrome, and the change read as a silent failure. It took removing the home-screen icon and re-adding it. **Symptom 2, which `black-translucent` causes:** every route to the viewport height then reports one status bar less than the screen. Measured: `screen.height` **874**, `documentElement.clientHeight` **812**, `window.innerHeight` **812**, `visualViewport.height` **812**, `env(safe-area-inset-top)` **62**, for a box anchored at y=0. The host, the `height: 100%` product div inside it and the `bottom: 0` tab bar all finished 62px short and the nav floated above a dead band. `100dvh`, `100vh`, `height: 100%` and `position: fixed` are all equally wrong here, because the initial containing block ITSELF is the short number — two attempted fixes changed nothing before that was measured rather than inferred. **Fix 2:** `.aa-mobile-viewport` adds `--aa-viewport-shortfall` to its height under `@media (display-mode: standalone)`; `MobileViewport` measures it against `screen.height` (the only source the bug does not touch) in a **`useLayoutEffect`**, so the corrected height is the first frame rather than a visible jump. The rule lives in `src/pwa/viewportMetrics.ts` with the evidence and seven Vitest cases. It is **derived, not hardcoded to `env(safe-area-inset-top)`**, so it cancels itself the day WebKit reports honestly; **clamped to the top inset**, so it can never do more damage than the bug; and **gated to standalone + WebKit**, because Android reports a comparable gap for its system bars and is not suffering this. **The trap for whoever touches it next:** once the correction is applied, `innerHeight` and `visualViewport.height` catch up to 874 while `clientHeight` stays 812. The rule therefore keys off `clientHeight` alone — against `innerHeight` it would compute a shortfall of 0, collapse the host, and loop. A regression test pins that fixed point. `pwa/index.html` keeps `overflow: hidden` on `html` ALONE for the same reason: a clipping `body` would cut the reclaimed strip off before it could paint. **Also shipped: a Viewport card in the More tab** (PWA only) carrying every measurement, the derived correction, a copy-diagnostics button, and a probe that paints the reclaimed strip so a screenshot proves it survives WebKit's clip. It exists because two rounds of this were debugged by measuring pixels off screenshots, which was slow and got the device model wrong. Delete it once the sizing has held across a few iOS releases. No domain, store, seed, lifecycle, billing or `PERSIST_VERSION` change.

- **2026-08-03 · Dock clearance is an in-flow `DockSpacer`, never trailing padding** (user-reported: a five-card list could not be scrolled, stranding "Add a card" behind the submit dock). **The cause is not iOS-specific and not the PWA work.** A scroll container's scrollable overflow is the union of its own padding box and its descendants' overflow, so `padding-bottom` creates no scrollable extent of its own — it only shows up once the CONTENT has already overflowed. Every mobile scroller reserved room for its floating dock or tab bar that way, so any screen whose content stopped just short of filling its scroller lost the reservation silently, put its last item under the chrome, and had nothing to scroll to bring it back. **Measured on St George's AM (5 cards, 402x874, real insets injected), same page, two engines:** WebKit 26.5 gave `clientHeight` 639 / `scrollHeight` **639** / scrollable **0**, Chromium gave 639 / 715 / 76. The two disagree on whether trailing padding joins the scrollable area and **WebKit has the better reading of the spec** — the layout was relying on the generous one, and the installed app only ever runs on the strict one. **Fix:** shared `DockSpacer` (`src/shared/ui/DockSpacer.tsx`), an in-flow `flex: none` block at the tail of the scroller, replacing the bottom padding on all six mobile scrollers (Lists, list detail, card detail, Availability, Balances, More). The clearance becomes real content, so it pushes the last item up and creates genuine scroll extent in every engine. Where the scroller is a flex column with a `gap`, the spacer is exactly that much shorter and the gap makes up the difference, so **every reserved total is unchanged** — verified by re-running the audit: the list detail now reports 715 / 76 under WebKit, identical to what Chromium always had. **This was only ever visible on one screen, but all six carried the same latent trap**, which is why all six changed rather than the reported one. `visual/mobile-insets.spec.ts` follows the clearance to its new home with a `clearance()` helper that reads the spacer's height and states the gap arithmetic per screen. Diagnosis used a throwaway Playwright probe under `browserName: 'webkit'` (the config pins Chromium for the shipped specs, deliberately); the probe is deleted, but note that **an engine-specific layout question needs the WebKit browser, not the Chromium the suite runs on**. No domain, store, seed, lifecycle, billing or `PERSIST_VERSION` change. `npm run build`, `npm run build:pwa`, **657** Vitest tests across 64 files and **87** Playwright specs all green.

## Discovered for later — handoff list

Small issues/ideas parked instead of scope-creeping. Phase 12 swept these into a prioritised handoff
for whoever builds the real system (or runs Phase 13). None is a demo blocker; all S1 to S5 run clean.
**Amended 2026-07-27:** items (P5) to (P9) were added by the conformance review. Still no demo
blocker and all S1 to S5 still run without error, but **(P6)** and **(P7)** are cases where the demo
script promises more than the staged data delivers, so "runs clean" no longer means "the narration
lands unaided" for the S5 audit beat and the S3 split-billing beat. **Follow-up, same day:** the
pre-workshop fix pass (Decisions log, 2026-07-27) resolved **(P6)** and **(P7)** — both scripted
beats now stage what the narration promises — and corrected **(P5)**'s copy; the repaint itself
remains open.

**What a real-build team should read FIRST:** this file's *Binding conventions* and *Decisions log*
(the readings we picked and why, with the settled rulings that must not be re-litigated), then
`docs/rfp-reference/RFP.md` + `Data-Model-and-Flow.md`, then `docs/demo-guide/` for the working mental
model. The prototype is a mock-backend demo (convention 4); the money/route/BTM maths in
`src/domain/billing/` is pure and the real reference. The §11 discovery items surfaced in the app UI
and the demo guide are the open questions to take to AA.

**Prioritised open items:**

1. **(P1) Holder-coherence advisory flag** (Phase 10+; NOT a Phase 09/12 work item, deferred again).
   The office contract picker offers every contract unfiltered and the billing run derives the
   counterparty FROM the resolved holder, so one wrong pick silently redirects an invoice (e.g. a
   billableParty-held contract on a hospital-route procedure bills the clinic on a patient layout). A
   `reviewFlags` advisory when the resolved holder is surprising for the route/list context, plus
   picker grouping, is the fix (8th review, fee-maths F10/O3).
2. **(P2) Type 3 second-procedure ordinal keying** (§11 discovery question). Whether a Type 3 price
   list must key second-procedure rows by `procedureOrdinal` (Phase 08's picked reading: an
   ordinal-agnostic row never prices an additional procedure and falls to BTM time-only) or whether
   some contracts intend a flat per-occurrence price. A question for AA.
3. **(P3) GST per-invoice rounding on split shares** (expected, not a bug). GST rounds per invoice,
   so a split procedure's summed GST can differ from the unsplit figure by a cent (e.g.
   $19.88 + $11.93 vs $31.80). Keep in mind when the Xero mirror reconciles totals (8th review O2).
4. **(P4) Type 2 percent-discount has no seeded end-to-end card.** It is implemented and pure-tested
   through the run (rate rounds to cents at derivation) but no seeded card exercises it end-to-end;
   seed one if a demo ever needs it.
5. **CLOSED 2026-10-09 (catch-up Phase 28): a phone booking assigns a List first, which shows in place of the session's status in all three apps and the finders.** **(P5) A Free List that receives an office phone booking is never repainted** (2026-07-27 review,
   finding 04.1; notable). `ListPatch` deliberately excludes `statusKey`
   (`src/store/lifecycle.ts:490-523`) and `PhoneAdviceBooking.tsx:68-72` patches only hospital,
   surgeon and times, so the List stays Free. Only the admin `DayGrid` derives a booked display: the
   web `WeekStrip` still renders it "Free / Open for cover" and non-clickable
   (`src/apps/web/components/WeekStrip.tsx:45,149`) and the dashboard day summary counts only
   private / public / preop Lists (`DashboardScreen.tsx:74-81`), so the booked Card is unreachable
   from **both** anaesthetist apps — while Beat 2 of `docs/demo-guide/03-demo-script.md:100-107` and
   `PhoneAdviceBooking`'s own docblock both assert it "appears immediately" there. Not blocking
   (Souter has no Free session on the design day, so the script cannot hit it), but the copy
   over-promises. Fix is either a status repaint on booking or honest copy.
   **Copy corrected 2026-07-27:** the script Expect line, the master HTML and the
   `PhoneAdviceBooking` docblock now describe the admin-grid truth; the anaesthetist-view repaint
   remains the open fix.
6. **(P6) The seeded audit trail is too thin for the beat scripted to showcase it** (2026-07-27

**Built:**

### Phase 08 — Billing engine: run & invoices (2026-07-23)

**Built:**
- **Pure domain** (`domain/billing/invoiceBuild.ts`, exported via the billing index): `GST_RATE` (labelled assumption), `resolveContractForProcedure` (stored-effective wins on the List date; scoped default-Type-1 fallback pre-filtered to `isDefault`; surgeon/organisation/billableParty-ineffective, dangling-contract and no-route cases → typed exceptions), `counterpartyForProcedure` (by HOLDER; insurer route → insurer; billableParty → typed payer else patient), `layoutFor`, and `buildInvoicesForCard` (rates each procedure via `feeContextFor` + `feeFor` with the RESOLVED contract substituted; funder-allocated procedures use the stored split verbatim after a billing-time conservation re-check vs the resolved-contract fee → `allocationStale`; price overrides land as a reason-carrying adjustment line so lines sum to the fee; groups by counterparty in first-appearance order; negative counterparty totals → exception; cancelled Cards → no invoices). `fee.ts` hardened in the review pass: percent-discount rates round to cents at derivation; an additional procedure takes a Type 3 fixed price only from an ordinal-keyed row. `validateCardForBilling` blocks overrides that drive the fee negative. `contracts.ts` exports `isEffectiveOn`.
- **Store** (`store/billingRun.ts`): `runBillingForList` — guards notFound/`listNotAuthorised`/`alreadyBilled`, builds every non-cancelled Card (each wrapped; per-card isolation absolute), then ONE atomic `mutate` as `{who: 'Billing run', role: 'system', source: 'system'}` writing invoices (`INV####`, invoiceNumber `AA-2026-####`, `caseReference` = its BillingCase id, `raisedAtISO`), lines (`IL####`, rate detail snapshotted into descriptions), cases (`BC####`; failures carry `failure: {code, message, procedureId?}`), and `List.billedAtISO` — audit metas `invoice.create`/`card.billed`/`card.billingException`/`list.billed`, every one `stampCardId: null`. `markInvoiceEmailed` (entity → uploadPortal → alreadyEmailed → officeOnly; audit `invoice.email`). `wireBillingRun` subscribed once in `main.tsx`; `emitAppEvent` now isolates listener errors. `mutate.ts` ID_FORMATS += invoice/invoiceLine/billingCase/invoiceNumber. Selectors: `billedLists`, `invoicesForList`, `invoiceLinesFor`, `invoiceCountsByList`, `counterpartyName` (Pick-narrowed so screens and `BillingLinesCard` share them). Guards hardened: `editContract` refuses forward-dating a protected default; `deleteContract` refuses a contract procedures still reference; `createHospital`'s auto-default is effective from the seed epoch.
- **Admin UI:** new **Invoices** side-nav section (`InvoicesScreen` — recently-billed strip, exceptions strip reading `case.failure`, invoices table with delivery status; inline detail, never a Dialog) and `InvoiceDocument` (`.aa-invoice-doc`: Logo masthead + serif TAX INVOICE, meta grid with case reference "internal reference only", contractHolder layout [Attn: Accounts + every distinct billingReference] vs patient layout [payment-category note per distinct category; billableParty shows "For the care of {patient}"], agency line on both, lines table, Subtotal/GST/Total due, GST-assumption caption; action bar outside the print node: Email → simulated-send badge, Print → `window.print()`, insurer → nib upload-portal stub, "Xero handoff pending · Phase 10" chip; refusals render verbatim). ### Phase 13 — Mobile atmospheric gradient & tuning lab (2026-07-24)
**Built:**
- **`src/theme/mobileGradient.ts`** — the pure, deterministic, CSS-only atmosphere module (no React/store/domain imports; no `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`): types (`MobileGradientConfig`/`GradientField`/`LowerFade`), `AA_DEFAULT_GRADIENT` referencing the existing `neutral.bg`/`accent.tint`/`brand.tint` tokens (no new design tokens), `isValidHex`/`normalizeHex`/`hexToRgba` (physical alpha clamp), `gradientCssVars` (stacked `linear-gradient` lower-fade over `radial-gradient` identity over `radial-gradient` accent; alpha = opacity × intensity; disabled fields omitted; master-off → image `none`; outer stops fade to the same colour at 0 alpha to avoid grey halos), `configToCssText` (Copy CSS), `serializeConfig`/`parseConfig` (stable key order, backfills partial input, ignores invalid hex/NaN), `envelopeWarnings` (advisory only), and guarded `loadStoredConfig`/`saveConfig` under `STORAGE_KEY='aa-gradient-lab'` / `STORAGE_VERSION=1`.
- **`src/theme/gradientLabGate.ts`** — the single named removable gate `GRADIENT_LAB_ENABLED = true` with a header explaining removal (flip to `false` or delete `src/shell/gradientLab/`; the atmosphere KEEPS working because it is sourced from `AA_DEFAULT_GRADIENT`, not the lab).
- **`src/shell/gradientLab/`** — `useGradientLab.ts` (`useMobileGradient()` → `{config, controller}`; gate-off ⇒ default config + null controller + localStorage never read; gate-on ⇒ persisted/live config + controller `{patch,setField,resetToDefault,panelOpen,setPanelOpen}`; hooks run unconditionally; persistence lives in an effect keyed on `config`, never a side effect inside the reducer); `AtmosphereLayer.tsx` (the single fixed `position:absolute; inset:0; zIndex:0` paint reading `var(--aa-atmos-*)`, `data-testid="mobile-atmosphere"` + `data-atmosphere` on/off); `GradientLab.tsx` (the outside-the-phone tuning panel); `index.ts` barrel; `gradientLabPurity.test.ts` (isolation guard).
- **`PhoneFrame.tsx`** (mobile-only; imported solely by `MobileApp`) — sets the `--aa-atmos-*` custom properties on the scaled device div (they inherit to every descendant incl. SlideStack), mounts `AtmosphereLayer` inside the device (behind the scrolling content, above the retained opaque `neutral.bg` fallback), and renders `<GradientLab>` as a `position:fixed` sibling in the grey outer canvas ONLY when the gate is on.
- **`MobileApp.tsx`** — app root `background: neutral.bg` → `transparent` (the atmosphere shows through for all four tabs and the Lists base). **`SlideStack.tsx`** — each layer `neutral.bg` → `background: var(--aa-atmos-base, #F6F8F7); backgroundImage: var(--aa-atmos-image, none)` (layers stay OPAQUE so a parked layer-behind at `translateX(-24%)` never shows through the active layer's gutters, but paint the SAME field, pixel-aligned with the fixed layer at rest → seamless push/pop, parallax intact); dropped the now-unused `neutral` import. White surfaces / the `CompletionOverlay` flood untouched; no translucency nudge to the tab bar or sticky footers was needed (no hard strip appeared).
- **The Gradient Lab** — a badged (`DemoBadge` "Gradient Lab" + muted "Temporary prototype control · tuning only" subtitle), keyboard-operable panel: master switch, global intensity (×), base colour (`<input type=color>` + editable hex), the two fields (accent teal / identity blush) each with enable + colour + X/Y anchor + horizontal/vertical spread + opacity + inner stop + fade, the lower neutral return (enable + start/end), a phone-proportioned live mini-preview, Reset to AA default, Copy configuration (stable JSON) and Copy CSS with transient "Copied" feedback, non-blocking envelope warnings, and invalid-hex handling that keeps the last valid preview. Starts collapsed behind a toggle button on every viewport (opened deliberately); when opened it docks in the left gutter, and on narrow (<1024) viewports it is capped to the measured gutter so it never covers the centred device.

**The checked-in default (design pass, `frontend-design` skill, iterated with the user):** (1) teal + weak-brand-blush two-tone → read as an unwanted red/green pairing; (2) a single calm teal hue → clean but carried none of the logo's crimson; (3) a soft brand-crimson family → the user chose the **faintest option, "Brand whisper"**, as the shipped default. **Final `AA_DEFAULT_GRADIENT`:** base `#F6F8F7`, intensity `1.0`, master on; single crimson-tint field `#ECCED5` (brand.base lightened ~78%; a brand-derived tint, NOT a new design token) at `34% / -20%`, spread `174% / 106%`, opacity `0.45`, fade `84%`; secondary field OFF; lower return `56%` → `96%`. The logo red is present as the barest ambient-identity haze, never a button or status colour, so the crimson-is-identity rule holds in spirit and teal stays the untouched action/status colour. Because the crimson-tint avatar would blend into the wash, the persona avatar was reworked to a shared **`Avatar`** component with an "elevated-white" treatment (white fill, crimson initials, the cards' `elevation.e1` shadow, no ring) — the user's pick from a standalone `avatar-options.html` comparison page — used for the header, More profile and "My availability" avatars.

**Preset switcher (user request):** the lab leads with a **`GRADIENT_PRESETS` grid of ten switchable ideas** (`src/theme/mobileGradient.ts`), now led by a brand-red family per the user's steer — five soft-crimson washes (brand dawn / crown / soft / warm / whisper, brand-base lightened ~72 to ~82% for a felt-to-gentle range), two teal options, the original teal+blush duo, a near-colourless neutral "mist", and a flat-white baseline. Each is a full config applied via `controller.applyPreset`; the active one is highlighted (deep-equal on the serialized config); every colour is a design token or a brand-derived tint and stays white-first. The two field controls were relabelled Primary / Secondary field (any hue in either).

**Persistence & gate:** lab state persists under its own key **`aa-gradient-lab`** (independent of the domain store `aa-demo` and the phone scale `aa-phone-scale`); Reset demo data (`resetDomainState`, `setState`-only) never touches it. The gate constant is **`GRADIENT_LAB_ENABLED`** in **`src/theme/gradientLabGate.ts`**.

**Deviations from plan:** (1) the header badge is a compact "Gradient Lab" `DemoBadge` plus a muted "Temporary prototype control · tuning only" subtitle rather than one long single-badge label — same meaning, but the full label wrapped to two ragged lines in the 300px header (review finding). (2) Radial outer stops fade to the field colour at 0 alpha (not the `transparent` keyword) to avoid a grey halo — a quality choice inside the recipe. (3) The narrow-open overlay is capped to the *measured* device left edge (the plan's "overlay the grey canvas, never the device viewport" realised via measurement). No scope fences crossed: only the in-phone canvas gains atmosphere; the outer `#E4E8E6` backdrop, device chrome, web/admin/demo apps, status/action/text tokens, `global.css` `@theme`, and all domain/seed/clock/audit/store code are untouched (`git diff` touches only PhoneFrame/MobileApp/SlideStack plus the new lab files).

**Manual test checklist:**
- ✓ `/mobile` at Fit / ~90% / ~100% / ~130% and a narrow viewport: subtle teal-top-left + weak-blush-top-right atmosphere behind all four tabs and every Lists depth; white cards and the CardDetail white header crisp; no seam/flash/restart on push-pop; fixed while scrolling (screenshot-verified).
- ✓ Web / admin / demo apps and the grey backdrop visually unchanged (they never import `PhoneFrame`; the `--aa-atmos-*` vars appear only in mobile-scoped files).
- ✓ Lab: master on/off flat-vs-atmosphere compare (`data-atmosphere` flips to `off`, image → `none`, card stays visible); tune both fields + intensity live (in-phone only, immediate); Reset to AA default restores the checked-in look; Copy configuration + Copy CSS produce readable, parseable content with feedback.
- ✓ A changed value persists across tab + List/Card navigation and a page reload; Reset demo data leaves the lab value intact (independent key).
- ✓ Narrow: panel collapses to a toggle button clear of the device and the zoom/Fit toolbar; opening keeps the panel in the left gutter, clear of the phone; app switcher never covered; no horizontal page scroll; no focus trap.
- ✓ `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) + `npx vitest run` (**488**, +31: 28 in `mobileGradient.test.ts` incl. preset coverage, 3 in `gradientLabPurity.test.ts`) + `npx oxlint` green; **39** Playwright specs pass (+2 in `mobile-phase13.spec.ts`, incl. a preset-switch check), console clean.

**Adversarial review-fix pass (convention 18):** 3 independent Opus lenses — visual-quality/accessibility · bugs/correctness · plan-adherence — read PROGRESS + the phase doc + the Design Language + the diff. No hard scope violations. Confirmed and fixed: **(both lenses) the OPEN lab panel overlapped the centred device on narrow viewports (L1)** — now capped to the measured left gutter, with a non-overlap assertion added to the narrow Playwright test; **(both lenses)** the mini-preview's landscape box misrepresented the phone's radial geometry — now a phone-proportioned portrait thumbnail; **(quality)** the hex input gained `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby` and the envelope warnings an `aria-live` region; the long badge label wrapped in the header (short badge + subtitle); the `WARN_INK` comment overclaimed ("NOT a status token") — reworded to state honestly it mirrors the warning-onTint value but is kept a plain literal so the lab has zero coupling to the status/domain token system; **(bugs)** `saveConfig` sat inside the `setState` updater (double-write under StrictMode) — moved to an effect keyed on `config`; the collapsed button flashed for one frame on wide load — `panelOpen` now seeds from the initial width (mount-once effect dropped). Verified-and-NOT-a-defect: a "missing `gradientLabPurity.test.ts`" finding was a false positive (the file exists; the reviewer wasn't given it); degenerate colour stops are reachable only via a non-wired `parseConfig` import path (the sliders are bounded); the Copy-CSS `.aa-mobile-atmosphere` rule is a portable template; `parseConfig` is planned public API; focus-on-toggle was left as-is (auto-focusing on load would be worse). Alpha maths, layer order, master-off path, nullish merges, storage isolation, clipboard error handling, stacking/z-index, and the SlideStack seam were all independently verified sound. Re-greened build + 484 Vitest + oxlint + 39 Playwright.

- *Fixed, with tests:* `editHospital` and `editSurgeonGroup` audited a save that changed nothing and re-logged unchanged fields (now only changed fields, members as a set, and no entry for no change); the candidate picker's first render after reopening used the previous opening's shuffle key and re-sorted a frame later (the key is now the bump's value from the first render); phone advice warned on a surgeon the List already had, where nothing is acknowledged (now only a changed surgeon warns, as in Edit list); `titledSurname` invented "Dr" for an untitled name.
- *Fixed (quality):* the store's same-side rule now calls `activeEntryOnSide`, the add sheet's helper; the refusal's kind words come from `PAIRING_LABELS`; anaesthetist names are links (keyboard); "Open record" is a link; one `textActionStyle` and a shared `FormError`; helper lines tied to their fields; `useId` for the section title; a dead class removed and the ended-entry link given the shared link style; History rows labelled per pairing; "None recorded." for an empty group; a neutral reason placeholder; `formatCurrency` on the record; the duplicated tier pill and HPI CPN row on the record removed; `mastersViewPath` typed; one `pairingSubject`; the unused `todayISO` prop dropped; a per-row Edit on Surgeons; the hospital email hint no longer implies the app sends email; a lint warning in a session-1 test.
- *Not changed:* the History buttons (the Audit viewer only summarises a change; the checklist's HPI CPN and "Asked by" rows are read there); the Anaesthetists table's raw GST period enum (older than this phase); the side radios' wording from `PAIRING_LABELS` (still the one label set).

- **Domain** (`domain/outOfHours.ts`): `OUT_OF_HOURS`, `OUT_OF_HOURS_DESIGN`, `OUT_OF_HOURS_LABEL`, `isOutOfHours`, `sessionText` (the one way a session is printed), `SESSIONS_IN_ORDER`, `sessionRank`/`compareSessions` (the one way sessions are ordered; every `localeCompare` on a session was replaced), `listsOnDay`, `openOutOfHoursRefusal`, `outOfHoursTimesRefusal` (start before end, and no earlier than the PM session ends).

- **Admin:** "Open out-of-hours session" in each row's new right gutter (`GRID_GUTTER` 40px; the ruler and the Draft Lists band end with it, the ruler's end hour labelled in the header's gutter so it reads 07:00 to 18:00, or to 21:00 on an evening), shown only when the pointer is over the gutter or on keyboard focus, never while a drawer or sheet is open, absent on a past day or a row that has one; `OpenOutOfHoursSheet` (session times, 18:00 to 21:00) lands on the session's drawer; the empty-session drawer adds "Draft Lists for this session" (`Assign here`) and, on an evening, "Close out-of-hours session"; the grid draws the evening block after PM (moon mark, `daygrid-evening-block`) on a ruler past 18:00 only on a day with an evening session or an evening Draft List, a quiet after-hours zone behind; Find available, Draft List and Change date offer "Out-of-hours"; Schedule settings show and edit the OOH default.
- **Anaesthetist apps:** sessions sort AM, PM, out-of-hours everywhere; `ListRow` shows a moon and the start for `OOH` with "Out-of-hours" leading the subtitle; the web Lists table, week strip, Who's free, availability grid (an Out-of-hours column on a day that has one, quiet empty cells), mobile availability (her evening and colleagues' where open), the day panel ("Change both sessions" kept) and the calendar labels all take it; her own List and Booking moves work on it into a colleague's opened free evening.

- *Confirmed and fixed (with tests):* renaming an other payer kept their BP id (a new person inherited the old one's Xero contact and could take their deposit) → a different name gets a new id; a split line to the patient carried the Booking's guardian's details → `billedToFor` and `invoiceDeliveryFor` read the invoice's own counterparty (`personDetailsFor`), and a payer no longer on the Booking resolves to no one; a payer change after a prepayment invoice stranded the balance run (`prepaidCounterpartyChanged`) → refused ("A prepayment invoice has already been raised to the current payer, so the payer cannot change."); issued invoices named by the live Booking (or "BP0001" where only masters were passed: Invoices, the billing lines card) → `invoiceAddresseeName` reads `billedTo` first everywhere; an office Clear on a staged child or approval warning stranded the sample → Clear and unstage no longer count as value changes; an unchanged payer save wrote an audit row and blocked the samples (JSON key order) → order-independent `sameData`; one hand edit on a redirected target blocked every sample → that sample is skipped with its real reason, and the approval target follows the seed's funder; History could not show a contact change → `payerContact` before and after; a surgeon group billed as itself (Unisports) was never asked for its reference while COS was → judged by Party kind; a funder whose Party changed kind could not be saved → an unchanged funder stays accepted; a malformed record email hid a typed one → `isEmailShaped` first, and only a well-formed email is snapshotted; the Payer row told the anaesthetist a holder pays (US-15.0.1) → office only, and the sheet's subtitle is one neutral line; the child hint showed for a holder-billed minor → gated as the warning; the add form claimed the record's contact for a new patient → shows the record's values or says none is on file; the anaesthetist saw a "Billing reference" with an "approval reference" placeholder → office only, "Hospital contract reference"; the funder chips were toggles → radios; the approval chip re-derived the rule → `approvalNumberMissing` passed in; insurance History read "Funder" (the funding tag label) → "Insurer or funder"; the blank row's link read "Add" → "Add insurer or funder"; `seed/billing.ts` would mislabel a payer contact → mapped as the history seed; stale "until Phase 21" comments; catalogue rows.
